archael-set.summary: A heavily enchanted elytra with no special ability of its own. Its value is the enchantments on it.

details.text: The set's code does nothing when events happen, so there is no hidden effect beyond the enchantments.
Enchantments: Protection VI, Projectile Protection V, Unbreaking V and Feather Falling IV, all on an elytra.

avalon-set.summary: Every Avalon piece makes you move faster while it's worn or held. Wear all four armor pieces together and you also get Speed I, refreshed every few seconds.

use.text: Any piece (armor, sword, pickaxe or rod): its speed bonus is set to apply in any equipment slot, so it works whether the piece is worn or held.
Full set: wear the Avalon helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots at the same time to get Speed I.

numbers.label: Speed bonus per piece
numbers.value: +0.025 movement speed

numbers.label: Full-set Speed I
numbers.value: 12 s (240 ticks), re-applied every 3.5 s while the full set is worn

details.text: The full-set check looks only at your four armor slots. Every slot has to hold an Avalon piece, so a missing piece or an elytra in the chest slot turns the Speed I bonus off.
Speed I isn't removed when you take a piece off. It runs out on its own, up to 12 s later.

blitz-set.summary: The Blitz Axe gives you Haste while you hold it. The Blitz Wings launch you forward each time you use a firework rocket while gliding.

use.text: Axe: hold it in your main hand to get Haste I, which is re-applied every 3.5 s.
Wings: wear them in the chest slot and use a firework rocket while gliding. You're thrown in the direction you're looking and an extra rocket-launch sound plays.

numbers.label: Haste I duration
numbers.value: 11 s (220 ticks), refreshed every 3.5 s

numbers.label: Rocket launch
numbers.value: sets your speed to 1.5 in your look direction

details.text: The launch doesn't cancel the rocket. The rocket is still used as normal on top of the launch.

quirks.text: The Haste check only asks whether your main-hand item is any axe. If you wear the Blitz Wings, or hold the Blitz Axe in your off-hand, any axe in your main hand gets Haste.

falter-set.summary: Falter tools deal bonus damage based on your level in the matching Job: pickaxe uses Miner, hoe uses Farmer, axe uses Lumberjack and fishing rod uses Fisherman.

use.text: Hit a mob or player while holding a Falter tool. The bonus is based on your level in the Job that matches your main-hand tool.

numbers.label: Bonus damage per hit
numbers.value: your Job level ÷ 4 (e.g. level 40 gives +10 damage)

details.text: If you haven't joined the matching Job, or your main-hand item isn't a pickaxe, hoe, axe or fishing rod, the bonus is 0.
Projectiles you shoot also count as your hits, but the Job is still chosen from your main-hand item. A bow in your main hand gives no bonus.

quirks.text: The tool only has to be the right type, not a Falter tool. With a Falter piece in your off-hand, a plain pickaxe in your main hand still gets the Miner bonus.

config.text: This needs the Jobs plugin, with Jobs named exactly Miner, Farmer, Lumberjack and Fisherman. How high levels go depends on the server's Jobs setup.

harbinger-set.summary: Wearing any single Harbinger piece, including the elytra, keeps Night Vision on you. You don't need the full set.

use.text: Wear at least one Harbinger piece in an armor slot. The elytra counts when it's in the chest slot.

numbers.label: Night Vision
numbers.value: 15 s (300 ticks), re-applied every 3.5 s while worn

details.text: Wearing more pieces doesn't make it stronger. It's always Night Vision I.
Night Vision stays for up to 15 s after you take the last piece off.

kazkan-set.summary: A combat set with a different trick on each piece. The axe charges up bonus damage while you hold right-click. The crossbow freezes arrows in mid-air so you can fire them later. The staff spends lapis to slow a mob or cast a damaging bolt.

use.text: Axe: hold right-click to charge, then hit something while you're still charging. The bonus only applies if your last right-click was less than 0.3 s ago.

Crossbow: each arrow you shoot slows to 1% of its speed and stops falling, so it hangs almost still in the air. Left-click with a crossbow to fire the oldest frozen arrow at the entity you're looking at, or straight ahead if you're not looking at one.
Staff: right-click while looking at a mob to give it Slowness XXXI. This costs 13 lapis and doesn't work on players.
Staff: left-click to cast a hidden bolt trailed by witch particles. It flies straight without dropping and damages the first living thing it hits. Costs 13 lapis.
Shield: it has no ability of its own. Holding it still turns on the set's other effects (see the notes below).

numbers.label: Axe charge
numbers.value: +1 damage for every 4 right-clicks registered while charging, up to +14 damage

numbers.label: Frozen arrows
numbers.value: up to 5 at once; a 6th makes the oldest start falling

numbers.label: Frozen arrow timeout
numbers.value: 7.5 s (150 ticks), after which an unfired arrow starts falling

numbers.label: Crossbow aim range / launch speed
numbers.value: locks onto a target within 75 blocks; fired at speed 3.2

numbers.label: Staff slow
numbers.value: Slowness XXXI for 10 s (200 ticks), target within 15 blocks, 13 lapis

numbers.label: Staff bolt
numbers.value: 17 damage (8.5 hearts) on hit, lasts 6 s (120 ticks), 13 lapis

details.text: Lapis can come from anywhere in your inventory. If you have fewer than 13, nothing happens and nothing is taken.
The bolt won't hurt anything the server's protection says you can't damage.
Frozen arrows lose their critical-hit status. An arrow fired with left-click is made a critical hit again.
Hitting something doesn't use up the axe charge. It keeps counting for as long as you keep holding right-click.

quirks.text: Every ability only checks what type of item is in your main hand while any Kazkan piece is in either hand. If you hold the Kazkan Shield in your off-hand, a regular axe charges, a regular crossbow fires frozen arrows, and arrows from a regular bow freeze in the air.

config.text: What the bolt is allowed to hit depends on the server's WorldGuard and Towny setup.

magmatic-set.summary: A fire-themed set. The sword shoots a flame bolt that sets mobs on fire. The pickaxe smelts ores as you mine them, and the shovel turns sand into glass. The armor has no ability beyond its enchantments.

use.text: Sword: right-click to fire a hidden bolt trailed by flames. Whatever living thing it hits catches fire.
Pickaxe (main hand): gold, iron and copper ore (including deepslate) and ancient debris drop ingots or netherite scrap instead of raw drops.
Shovel (main hand): sand and red sand drop glass.
Armor: no special ability.

numbers.label: Flame bolt cooldown
numbers.value: 10 s (200 ticks)

numbers.label: Burn time on hit
numbers.value: 5 s (100 ticks)

numbers.label: Bolt lifetime
numbers.value: 6 s (120 ticks)

numbers.label: Bonus XP per smelted ore
numbers.value: 1 XP orb (worth 1)

details.text: The drops are worked out from the pickaxe you're holding first, then turned into ingots.
The flame bolt won't ignite anything the server's protection says you can't damage.
Abilities are switched off in the newer event world, and you get a one-time action-bar notice about it.

quirks.text: The flame bolt works with any sword in your main hand, as long as a Magmatic item is in one of your hands. For example, the Magmatic Pickaxe in your off-hand and a plain sword in your main hand fires bolts.

meluka-set.summary: A water set. The armor gives you Dolphin's Grace while you're in water. The pickaxe and shovel put blocks you break straight into your inventory, but only while you're in water.

use.text: Armor: wear any one piece while in water to get Dolphin's Grace. You don't need the full set.
Pickaxe or shovel (main hand): while you are in water, the drops from blocks you break go into your inventory instead of onto the ground.

numbers.label: Dolphin's Grace
numbers.value: 12 s (240 ticks), re-applied every 3.5 s while you're in water

details.text: It checks whether you are in water, not the block you break. Breaking a block underwater from dry land doesn't trigger it.
Only item drops are moved to your inventory. Experience from the block isn't touched.

quirks.text: The set is marked as disabled in the newer event world, but that only turns off the tool pickup there. Dolphin's Grace from the armor still works, because the timer that grants it skips the world check.

reforged-set.summary: Each Reforged piece adds one extra heart of max health while worn in its own slot. The bonus adds up, so the full set gives four extra hearts. There is no other ability.

use.text: Wear the pieces in their normal armor slots. Each piece's bonus only counts in its own slot.

numbers.label: Max health per piece
numbers.value: +2 (1 heart)

numbers.label: Full set
numbers.value: +8 max health (4 hearts)

details.text: Each piece has its own separate health bonus, so they stack, and the netherite armor values are kept.

valley-set.summary: A golden farming and utility set. The shovel deletes water you look at from a distance, the sword buffs you when you hit monsters, and the hoe sometimes drops bonus crops. The axe and fishing rod have no special ability.

use.text: Shovel: left- or right-click while looking at water to remove that one water block.
Sword: hitting a monster gives you Speed I and Resistance I.
Hoe (main hand): any block you break has a small chance to drop a bonus wheat or golden carrot.
Axe and fishing rod: no special ability.

numbers.label: Water removal reach
numbers.value: 45 blocks

numbers.label: Sword buffs
numbers.value: Speed I + Resistance I for 5 s (100 ticks)

numbers.label: Hoe bonus crop chance
numbers.value: 3% per block broken (50/50 wheat or golden carrot, 1 item)

details.text: The sword buffs only trigger when the thing you hit counts as a monster. Hitting animals or players does nothing.
Only the first block you're looking at is checked, and it's only removed if that block is water itself.

quirks.text: The shovel and sword abilities only check what type of item is in your main hand. With any Valley piece in your off-hand, a regular shovel removes water and a regular sword grants the buffs.

config.text: Removed water is logged to CoreProtect or Prism if the server runs one of them.

venom-set.summary: Viper gear poisons things in combat. The tooltips split the effects between weapons and armor, but in the code every piece does both: whatever you hit is poisoned, and so is whatever hits you.

use.text: Wear or hold any Viper piece. Anything you damage is poisoned, including targets hit by arrows or other projectiles you shoot.
Wear or hold any Viper piece. A mob or player that hits you in melee is poisoned.

numbers.label: Poison
numbers.value: Poison II for 3 s (60 ticks), each time

details.text: If another plugin has already cancelled the hit, no poison is applied.
Wearing more pieces doesn't make the poison stronger or longer. It's just applied again.

quirks.text: Against the tooltips, the armor also poisons what you hit, and a held Viper Sword or Axe also poisons what hits you.
Ranged attackers are never poisoned. The poison only goes to an attacker that is itself a living creature, so a hit from an arrow or other projectile is skipped.

verdant-set.summary: Verdant armor keeps Regeneration on you while you wear any single piece. The pickaxe, hoe and shovel refill a little hunger for every block you break. Despite its tooltip, the axe doesn't.

use.text: Armor: wear any one piece to get Regeneration I. You don't need the full set.
Pickaxe, hoe or shovel (main hand): each block you break restores 1 hunger point. If your hunger bar is already full, it adds saturation instead.

numbers.label: Regeneration I
numbers.value: 12 s (240 ticks), re-applied every 3.5 s while worn

numbers.label: Per block broken
numbers.value: +1 hunger point, or +0.5 saturation when hunger is full (up to 20)

details.text: Wearing more armor pieces doesn't make Regeneration stronger. It stays at level I.

quirks.text: The Verdant Axe never restores hunger even though its tooltip says it does. The hunger ability only runs for items the plugin treats as tools, and it classes every axe as a weapon.

zephyr-skates.summary: Netherite boots that give you a short, fast dash when you start sneaking while walking on solid ground. The dash goes in the direction you were last moving, not where you're looking.

use.text: Walk on solid ground (not flying or gliding), then press sneak. You're shoved hard in the direction you were moving, slightly downward.

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 1 s (20 ticks) between dashes

numbers.label: Dash strength
numbers.value: horizontal speed of up to 5 (a very strong push), with a slight downward pull

numbers.label: Hunger cost
numbers.value: 50% chance per dash to take 1 saturation, or 1 hunger point if saturation is below 1

details.text: "Grounded" means the block half a block below your feet is solid. You also have to have moved since your last sneak, because each sneak uses up the stored direction.

quirks.text: The movement and sneak checks never look at your boot slot, so the dash also works with the skates held in either hand.

clown-mask.summary: A wearable head that gives +3 hearts when worn. Right-clicking it puts it straight on your head.

use.text: Right-click while holding it to put it on, but only if your helmet slot is empty.

numbers.label: Max health
numbers.value: +6 (3 hearts), head slot only

config.text: Each mask gets a random face when it's created, picked from a list of textures in the server's heads config.

magicians-cloak.summary: An elytra that stores up the damage you deal as stars, one star per 120 damage. With at least one star, right-click a mob while holding a weapon or tool to spend all your stars on a delayed, explosive attack.

use.text: Charge it by damaging mobs or players. Melee hits and your own projectiles both count, and the action bar shows your stars.
Right-click while looking at a living target and holding a weapon or tool in your main hand (sword, axe, bow, crossbow, trident, mace, spear, pickaxe, shovel, hoe, fishing rod or shears).

numbers.label: Charge per star
numbers.value: 120 damage dealt (each hit rounded down to a whole number)

numbers.label: Charge cap
numbers.value: stops charging once you reach 5 stars (600 damage)

numbers.label: Spell damage
numbers.value: 20 per star, split into 5 hits half a second apart

numbers.label: Targeting range
numbers.value: 50 blocks

numbers.label: Target slowdown
numbers.value: Slowness IV for 2.5 s; the target is also frozen in place on each hit

numbers.label: Final explosion
numbers.value: power equal to your star count, no fire, no block damage

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 5 s (100 ticks) after a release. No charge is gained during it

details.text: Releasing resets the charge to zero. Nothing happens without at least 1 star, or if you aren't allowed to hurt the target (claims and protection plugins are respected).

quirks.text: The cap only stops charging once you're already at 600 or more, so the last hit can push you past 5 stars. A very big final hit can give a release stronger than 5 stars.

snowy-sunset-wings.summary: An elytra that makes you glow while worn in the chest slot, with a black outline if the server's glow-colour plugin is installed.

numbers.label: Glowing
numbers.value: 17 s (340 ticks), topped up every 3.5 s while worn

quirks.text: Taking the wings off removes every Glowing effect you have, including one from a spectral arrow or another item.

config.text: The black outline colour only works when the LumaGlowAPI plugin is present. Without it you get the default white glow.

flourishing-fedora.summary: A netherite helmet that sometimes makes everything with growth stages around you grow by one stage.

numbers.label: Chance
numbers.value: 6% every 3.5 s

numbers.label: Radius
numbers.value: about 5 blocks around you

numbers.label: Growth per trigger
numbers.value: +1 stage on every growing block in range

details.text: It affects any block that has growth stages, not just farm crops. Fully grown blocks are skipped.
Claims aren't checked, so crops on other players' land within range grow too.

quirks.text: The code never checks that the fedora is on your head, so it also works while held in either hand.

wizards-hat.summary: An unbreakable leather hat that gives +3 hearts when worn and keeps switching between four colours.

numbers.label: Max health
numbers.value: +6 (3 hearts), head slot only

numbers.label: Colour change
numbers.value: every 3.5 s while worn, random pick from 4 colours

details.text: It really is unbreakable. "Revitalise" has no code beyond the extra hearts.

wonder-beanie.summary: A netherite helmet with +2 hearts. While it's worn, potion effects you get from potions, tipped arrows, lingering clouds, totems, axolotls or dolphins last longer and are 1 or 2 levels stronger.

numbers.label: Max health
numbers.value: +4 (2 hearts), head slot only

numbers.label: Extra duration
numbers.value: +10 to 20 s (random)

numbers.label: Extra level
numbers.value: +1 or +2 (random)

details.text: Only these sources are boosted: drinking or splashing a potion, lingering clouds, tipped arrows, totems, axolotls and dolphins. Food (golden apples, stews), beacons and conduits are not.

quirks.text: Harmful effects count too. Poison or Slowness from an enemy's tipped arrow or splash potion is also made longer and stronger.

carnival-lollipop.summary: Holding the lollipop gives you Speed I and Haste I. It can't be placed like a normal flower.

numbers.label: Effects
numbers.value: Speed I + Haste I, 13 s each, topped up every 3.5 s

details.text: Works in either hand. The effects stay up to 13 s after you put it away.
Placing it is blocked.

book-of-knowledge.summary: A spellbook with two spells: Drain, which pulls health from everything around you, and Valiant Explosion, a spell ball that wears down and then blows up the mob it hits. Holding it also adds 1 XP to every orb you pick up.

use.text: Right-click to cast the selected spell. Left-click (book in main hand), or sneak + right-click, switches spells. The new spell is shown in chat.
Drain: every living thing within 15 blocks that you're allowed to hurt takes 1 heart per pulse, and you heal 1 heart for each one hit.

Valiant Explosion: fires a spell ball. If it hits a mob you're allowed to hurt, the mob loses a third of its current health, is frozen with extreme Slowness, then explodes at the 2 s mark (only if you can build at that spot).

numbers.label: XP bonus
numbers.value: +1 XP per orb picked up while held

numbers.label: Drain
numbers.value: 6 pulses, 1 s apart; 2 damage per target and 2 healing per target each pulse; 15-block range

numbers.label: Valiant damage
numbers.value: 1/3 of the target's current health, in 4 hits half a second apart

numbers.label: Valiant slow
numbers.value: Slowness LI for 2 s

numbers.label: Valiant explosion
numbers.value: power 20, sets fire, doesn't break blocks

numbers.label: Spell ball lifetime
numbers.value: 7.5 s (150 ticks)

details.text: Drain picks its targets when you cast it. That can include passive mobs and players, as long as protection rules let you damage them.
While a spell is on cooldown, casting it does nothing and shows no message.

quirks.text: Valiant Explosion's cooldown only starts when the ball hits a mob you're allowed to hurt. A ball that misses doesn't start it.

windforged-rocket.summary: A firework rocket that never runs out. It refills itself after each use, but only works 3 times in any 30 seconds and backfires in the Nether.

use.text: Right-click like a normal rocket (e.g. to boost while gliding). If the rocket was used up, a fresh one appears in the same hand a tick later.

numbers.label: Uses
numbers.value: 3 per rolling 30 s window

numbers.label: Nether penalty
numbers.value: Poison I for 6 s, and that use is blocked

details.text: When it's resting, the action bar shows how many seconds are left and the use is blocked.
A Nether use still counts toward your 3.
Right-clicking a shelf block doesn't count as a use.

quirks.text: Every right-click with it, in the air or on a block, counts as one of your 3 uses. The code doesn't check whether you're gliding.

winter-vault.summary: A breeze rod that launches you high into the air when you right-click.

numbers.label: Launch
numbers.value: adds 1.5 upward, then multiplies your whole speed by 2.45

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 15 s (300 ticks)

details.text: Your current horizontal speed is multiplied too, so vaulting while running also throws you forward.
It fires on any right-click while it's in either hand.
Nothing protects you from fall damage.
Doesn't work in the new event world (worlds:event_new).

carnival-fishing-rod.summary: An unbreakable Lure III event rod that can't actually fish. Every fishing action with it is cancelled, from either hand.

details.text: Everything it does as a fishing rod is cancelled.

config.text: Nothing in LumaItems gives it a use. Any purpose it has on the server would come from somewhere else.

carnival-pickaxe.summary: An unbreakable Efficiency II event pickaxe that can't break blocks or interact with anything. All its clicks and block breaks are cancelled.

details.text: Left-clicks, right-clicks, other interactions and block breaks are all cancelled.

quirks.text: The click blocking also applies with the pickaxe in your off-hand, so it can stop you using your main-hand item.

config.text: Nothing in LumaItems gives it a use. Any purpose it has on the server would come from somewhere else.

carnival-crossbow.summary: An unbreakable event crossbow (Quick Charge II, Infinity) that can't fire. Every projectile launch is cancelled while it's in hand.

quirks.text: The block covers anything you launch, not just its own bolts. With it in your off-hand, you can't throw or shoot other things (pearls, snowballs, tridents, bows) either.

config.text: Nothing in LumaItems gives it a use. Any purpose it has on the server would come from somewhere else.

christmas-charm.summary: A collectible from the Christmas minigames with no special ability. Its item code has no ability at all, whatever the lore hints.

config.text: The lore suggests keeping it for later, but nothing in LumaItems reads it. Any future use would have to come from elsewhere.

circus-harrower.summary: A netherite hoe that harvests mature crops around you one at a time when you sneak and right-click.

use.text: Sneak + right-click while standing among fully grown crops. It breaks them one by one and they drop as if broken with the item in your main hand (Fortune IV if that's the harrower).

numbers.label: Area
numbers.value: flat rings out to 4 blocks from you, at your feet level

numbers.label: Speed
numbers.value: 1 crop every 0.25 s (5 ticks)

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 20 s (400 ticks), starting after the last crop is harvested

details.text: Harvests fully grown wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroots, nether wart and cocoa. It doesn't replant.
If there are no ripe crops nearby, nothing happens and no cooldown starts.

quirks.text: Melons and pumpkins are on its crop list but never get harvested, because the ripeness check rejects them.
The first ripe crop it finds is used for the claim check and then skipped, so one crop is always left standing. With only one ripe crop nearby, nothing is harvested but the cooldown still starts.
Claims are only checked for that one crop. The other crops it harvests aren't checked.
The rings are sampled at fixed angles, so a couple of spots inside the circle are never checked.

snowflake-harrower.summary: A netherite hoe that tills in a plus shape. Right-click dirt and the four blocks beside it become farmland along with the one you clicked.

details.text: The item itself only turns the four side neighbours (north, south, east, west) into farmland. The block you clicked is left to the normal hoe action.
Only dirt-named blocks and grass blocks with air above them are tilled. Dirt, coarse dirt, rooted dirt and grass work; podzol, mycelium and dirt paths don't.
No cooldown.

quirks.text: The four extra blocks aren't checked against claims.
It also works with the harrower in your off-hand, whatever you right-click with.

big-swing-axe.summary: A netherite axe with 2 extra blocks of reach and much slower mining and attacks. The large vertical area-break in its lore isn't in the code.

numbers.label: Reach
numbers.value: +2 blocks for blocks and mobs (main hand)

numbers.label: Attack speed
numbers.value: 0.6 per second (-3.4, replacing the axe's normal speed)

quirks.text: The lore promises breaking blocks in a large vertical area, but the item has no block-breaking code. It's only slower mining and more reach. (The Big Swing Spade does have its area break.)
The mining and attack slowdowns apply in any slot, so holding it in your off-hand slows your main-hand mining and attacks too.

frostbark-chisel.summary: A netherite axe that changes what shape logs drop as when you chop them: normal logs, stripped logs, wood (bark on all sides) or stripped wood.

use.text: Sneak + right-click to cycle the mode: Logs, Stripped Logs, Wood, Stripped Wood. The action bar shows the new mode, and the choice is saved on the axe.
Break a log or nether stem with the axe in your main hand. It drops in the selected form.

details.text: Supported wood types: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, warped and crimson. Other types (e.g. pale oak) drop normally.
It keeps the wood type. It doesn't turn oak into another tree.

quirks.text: Logs that are already stripped always drop as themselves, whatever the mode.

cinnamon-oxidizer.summary: A netherite pickaxe (copper-pickaxe look) that turns an unwaxed copper block into its next weathering stage just as you break it.

details.text: Works on any copper block that can still weather further. Waxed and fully oxidized copper aren't affected.
It only reacts to breaks that go through, so claims are respected.

quirks.text: The swap uses the next stage's default form, so shape details like stair direction or a double slab aren't carried over.

config.text: The block is swapped to the next stage in the middle of your break, and the break isn't cancelled. Whether you end up with the weathered block as your drop depends on how the game finishes the break (not tested).

violet-garnet-mattock.summary: A netherite pickaxe for amethyst geodes. Breaking a cluster or bud (or a block touching one) also breaks a whole sphere of pickaxe blocks around it, and budding amethyst you break yourself drops as an item.

use.text: Break an amethyst cluster or bud, or any block touching one on a face. Everything in the sphere around it that a pickaxe mines best is also broken.
Break budding amethyst directly to get it as an item.

numbers.label: Area
numbers.value: sphere with a 3-block radius around the broken block

numbers.label: Durability
numbers.value: 1 per extra block broken

details.text: Blocks in the area break only if a shovel, axe, shears or hoe wouldn't mine them faster, plus gravel, dirt, rooted dirt and clay. So stone and ores break; wood doesn't. Non-solid blocks are skipped.
Containers, spawners, bedrock, portal frames, signs, shulker boxes, farmland and similar blocks are never broken.
Blocks broken in the area drop as if mined with the mattock (Silk Touch).

quirks.text: The extra blocks in the area aren't checked against claims.
Budding amethyst inside the area is left alone because it's on the protected list. Only the budding block you break directly drops.

aquamax-angler.summary: A fishing rod that reels in a live sea creature instead of a normal catch. Each catch is swapped for a random water mob that's flung toward you.

details.text: The mob is random: anything in Minecraft's built-in "aquatic" mob group, or a Drowned or Frog. It spawns at the bobber and is thrown toward you.
The normal fish or treasure item is deleted.
Works from either hand.

quirks.text: The mob can be hostile (e.g. a Drowned), so a catch can start a fight.

frosted-alluring.summary: A fishing rod that reels itself in the moment a fish bites.

numbers.label: Reaction time
numbers.value: 1 tick after the bite

details.text: It fakes a right-click with the hand holding the rod (off-hand if it's there, otherwise main hand).

config.text: Needs the ProtocolLib plugin. Without it, bites aren't auto-reeled.

rimelure-rod.summary: A fishing rod where fish reach your hook much faster once they appear, and a catch sometimes comes as a pair.

numbers.label: Fish approach time
numbers.value: cut to 25% of normal

numbers.label: Pair chance
numbers.value: about 8.9% (9 in 101) per catch

details.text: Pairing adds 1 to the caught item. It only works on stackable catches, not rods, books or gear.

quirks.text: Neither effect works if you're holding a fishing rod in both hands.

winter-pruners.summary: Shears that instantly break glass blocks and mob heads with a left-click.

details.text: Works on any block whose name ends in GLASS (plain, stained and tinted glass, but not panes), on mob and player heads, and on skeleton or wither skeleton skulls.

quirks.text: Wall-mounted skeleton and wither skeleton skulls aren't matched. Wall-mounted mob heads are.
The name check also catches an extended piston's head, so left-clicking one breaks it right away.
It also triggers with the pruners in your off-hand.

config.text: The break uses the game's own "player breaks this block" action, which should go through claim protection and use your main-hand tool (so Silk Touch keeps the glass). That part depends on the game, not tested.

big-swing-spade.summary: A netherite shovel that digs out a wide oval of shovel blocks around each block you break, in exchange for very slow mining and attacks. It won't work while you have Haste.

numbers.label: Area
numbers.value: oval about 8 blocks wide, 6 deep and 4 tall around the broken block (2 below it, only 1 above)

numbers.label: Attack speed
numbers.value: 0.6 per second (-3.4)

details.text: The oval is wider side to side than it is deep, based on which way you face.
It only starts when you break a shovel block with the spade in your main hand. It only takes solid shovel blocks and skips blacklisted ones such as farmland and dirt paths.
If you have Haste, breaking a block removes your Haste instead of area-digging and shows "Cannot be used with Haste."
Extra blocks drop as if dug with the spade (Silk Touch) and cost no durability.

quirks.text: The extra blocks aren't checked against claims.
The slow mining and attack speed apply in any slot, including your off-hand.

crystalline-spade.summary: A diamond shovel that turns gravel and clay into one random stained glass block instead of their normal drops.

details.text: Each gravel or clay block gives exactly 1 stained glass block in a random one of the 16 colours. Flint, clay balls and the clay block itself never drop.
Must be in your main hand.

montanaire-spade.summary: The bundle opens into a Montanaire Spade of a random colour. The spade turns sand and red sand into concrete powder of its colour.

use.text: Right-click the bundle to use it up and get a spade.
Break sand or red sand with the spade in your main hand to get concrete powder instead.

numbers.label: Colours
numbers.value: 16 (every concrete powder colour), picked at random when the spade is made

numbers.label: Drop
numbers.value: 1 concrete powder per sand block

details.text: You can't choose the colour. It's rolled when the bundle is opened and saved on that spade.

abominable-howitzer.summary: A bow that fires small snow golems instead of arrows. They explode when they bump into something.

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 1 s (20 ticks). Shots during it are cancelled

numbers.label: Explosion
numbers.value: power 2.4, no fire, no block damage

numbers.label: Snowman
numbers.value: half size, 50% chance to have no pumpkin

details.text: The snowman explodes when any non-air block is right next to it sideways, or when it tries to leave a snow trail.

quirks.text: Any mob you kill while holding the Howitzer in either hand drops nothing and gives no XP, even if you killed it with something else.
If the snowman dies before either of those happens, it just disappears without exploding.

config.text: The blast has no owner and the code doesn't check claims or PvP. Whether nearby players (including you) are hurt depends on the server's protection settings.

candy-cannon.summary: A crossbow whose shots look like flying wool candy and deal 5 damage from the cannon to whatever living thing they hit.

numbers.label: Hit damage
numbers.value: 5 (2.5 hearts) to the living thing hit, credited to you

numbers.label: Max flight time
numbers.value: 15 s (300 ticks), then the shot is removed

details.text: Each shot is hidden from you and followed by a tiny red, orange or yellow wool block with a matching dust trail.
The shot is removed as soon as it hits anything.

quirks.text: This happens to anything you launch while the cannon is in either hand, not just its own bolts. A trident thrown this way is deleted when it hits, so it's lost. Ender pearls and other projectiles are deleted on impact too.

deorium-cutlass.summary: A netherite sword that creates a gravity well on the block you're looking at. The well pulls things in and damages and weakens mobs near its centre.

use.text: Right-click while looking at a block. The well appears one block above it.

numbers.label: Target range
numbers.value: 50 blocks

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 30 s (600 ticks)

numbers.label: Duration
numbers.value: 6 s, pulsing every 0.25 s

numbers.label: Pull range
numbers.value: 10 blocks

numbers.label: Core damage
numbers.value: 5 per pulse to living things within 2.5 blocks, plus Weakness II for 2 s

details.text: Players and armor stands are never pulled or hurt. Dropped items and other non-living things are pulled in too.
Disabled at spawn, in the piñata world and in the new event world.

quirks.text: The protection check only looks at one nearby entity each pulse. If that one is protected, the whole well collapses, even if other targets aren't protected.

config.text: Pulses come every 0.25 s, faster than the game's usual short hit protection after taking damage, so a mob in the core may not take all 5 damage every pulse. That depends on the game, not tested.

training-katana.summary: A netherite sword that looks like a wooden sword and attacks very fast. Left-click shoots a snowball; right-click puts a damage-over-time curse on a target, but gives you Darkness as well.

use.text: Left-click to launch a snowball that flies straight (no gravity), with sweep particles for its first few ticks.
Right-click while looking at a living target within 10 blocks. Both of you get Darkness, and the target takes damage every 1.25 s.

numbers.label: Attack speed
numbers.value: 8 per second (+4, replacing the sword's normal speed)

numbers.label: Curse damage
numbers.value: 3 damage every 1.25 s, 12 times over about 14 s (36 total before armor)

numbers.label: Darkness
numbers.value: Darkness II for 7.5 s, on you and the target

quirks.text: Right-click has no cooldown. Each use starts its own damage timer.
The code gives the snowball no extra damage; it hits like a normal thrown snowball.

yukon-cutlass.summary: A netherite sword that knocks loot out of mobs while you fight them. The first 3 hits on each mob roll its drops and spray them out as bouncing snowballs, but mobs you kill drop no stackable items.

use.text: Hit a mob with the cutlass in your main hand. Each of the first 3 hits rolls its loot and throws each stackable item out as a bouncing snowball.

numbers.label: Loot hits
numbers.value: 3 per mob (stored on the mob)

details.text: Loot snowballs bounce off blocks. They turn into a dropped item when they hit an entity or settle on top of a block. Before their first bounce, landing in water or lava also turns them into an item.
Unstackable loot (gear, tools) is never thrown out, but still drops normally on death.
Baby animals, the Ender Dragon, Wither, Elder Guardian and Warden are excluded.
Disabled in the special world (worlds:special).

quirks.text: The no-drops-on-kill rule doesn't check your main hand. Any mob you kill with the cutlass anywhere in your hands (even off-hand, killed with another weapon) loses its stackable drops.
A mob you've hit with the cutlass is marked. If it later dies without a player getting the kill, it also loses its stackable drops.

giant-inflatable-hammer.summary: A mace whose smash attacks stun the target, and sometimes knock out the ground under it.

numbers.label: Stun (mobs)
numbers.value: Slowness XI + Darkness II for 7.5 s

numbers.label: Stun (players)
numbers.value: Darkness II for 7.5 s (no Slowness)

numbers.label: Ground break chance
numbers.value: 10% per smash

numbers.label: Ground break area
numbers.value: 7 blocks in a small patch just under the target

details.text: Only smash attacks (hits after a fall) count, with the hammer in your main hand. Normal swings do nothing extra.
The ground break needs build permission at the target's position, and broken blocks drop as items.

quirks.text: Build permission is only checked at the target's own block, not for each block broken.

heavy-bloblob-scythe.summary: A slow, heavy netherite scythe. A fully charged swing or hit also fires a fan of 5 icy blobs that bounce off walls and hit hard. The extra-loot ability in its lore doesn't work.

use.text: Swing at the air or a block, or hit something, once your attack is at least 83% charged. Five blobs fly out in a fan in front of you.

numbers.label: Blob damage
numbers.value: 18 (9 hearts) per blob; each blob resets the target's hit cooldown so several can land

numbers.label: Spread
numbers.value: 5 blobs at -10, -5, 0, +5, +10 degrees, plus up to ±5 degrees random aim

numbers.label: Blob cooldown
numbers.value: 1.25 s (25 ticks)

numbers.label: Attack speed
numbers.value: about 0.55 per second (-3.45)

numbers.label: Blob life
numbers.value: up to 10 s per flight; bounces keep 75% speed while within 30 blocks of you

details.text: Blobs only hurt things you're allowed to damage (claims and PvP rules are respected) and never damage you. After a bounce, they vanish in liquid.

quirks.text: "Naturality" (extra drops from naturally spawned mobs) never adds anything. The extra loot it rolls is thrown away instead of being added to the mob's drops.
The blob fan also fires with the scythe in your off-hand when you swing or hit with something else.

frozenflare-shield.summary: A shield that sets off a big explosion around you if you're still sneaking 2 seconds after right-clicking or pressing sneak.

use.text: Right-click (e.g. raise the shield) or press sneak, then be sneaking 2 seconds later. The explosion goes off at your position.

numbers.label: Delay
numbers.value: 2 s (40 ticks)

numbers.label: Explosion
numbers.value: power 7, no fire, no block damage

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 15 s (300 ticks)

quirks.text: Despite the lore, it never checks that you're blocking. It only checks that you're sneaking at the 2-second mark, so sneaking alone is enough.

config.text: Claims and PvP aren't checked by the item. Whether other players are hurt depends on the server's protection settings.

liquorice-lorica.summary: A netherite chestplate that makes you walk a little faster and fly 25% faster (creative or /fly flight) while you wear it.

numbers.label: Walking speed
numbers.value: +0.025 movement speed while worn in the chest slot

numbers.label: Flight speed
numbers.value: 0.125 while worn (normal is 0.1), so 25% faster

details.text: The flight speed is set when you put the chestplate on or take it off.

quirks.text: Taking it off always resets your flight speed to the default 0.1, even if something else had given you a different flight speed.

config.text: The speed it changes is the game's creative-style flying speed, so it should only matter when flying in creative or with /fly, not when gliding with an elytra. This depends on the game, not tested.

harewear-glasses.summary: A netherite helmet that lets you look inside a shulker box without placing it. Sneak and right-click while holding the box.

use.text: Sneak and right-click with a shulker box in either hand. The box's contents open in a window titled with the box's name (or "Shulker Box" if it has none), and the box is not placed.

details.text: The window is view-only. Every click inside it is cancelled, so you can't take items out or put items in.

quirks.text: The glasses don't have to be on your head. The right-click check also runs for items in your hands, so holding the glasses in your off-hand and the box in your main hand works too.

pride-crown.summary: A crown you wear on your head. It gives 3 extra hearts and shows rainbow sparkles above you.

use.text: Right-click while holding it in your main hand to put it on. This only works if your helmet slot is empty. You can also click it into the helmet slot in your inventory.

numbers.label: Max health
numbers.value: +6 (3 hearts) while on your head

numbers.label: Sparkle interval
numbers.value: Every 3.5 s (70 ticks) while worn

details.text: The sparkles only show while the crown is on your head. Holding it doesn't show them.

bouquet-trousers.summary: Netherite leggings with a mid-air double jump. Start sneaking while you're in the air to launch forward and up. This works once per trip into the air, and landing from that jump is safe if you fell less than 10 blocks.

use.text: While you're about a block or more above solid ground, start sneaking to boost in the direction you're looking.

numbers.label: Boost
numbers.value: 0.6 × your look direction, with 0.7 upward speed

numbers.label: Walking speed
numbers.value: +0.025 movement speed while worn as leggings

numbers.label: Fall protection
numbers.value: Fall damage cancelled if the fall was under 10 blocks (only after a double jump)

details.text: You get one double jump each time you're in the air. It comes back when you touch the ground again.
It doesn't work in water or while flying.

quirks.text: The tooltip says "while falling", but the code only checks that you're off the ground. It also works on the way up from a normal jump.
The double jump and the fall protection aren't tied to wearing the leggings. Holding them in either hand works too. The speed bonus only counts while they're worn.

fishing-collectibles.summary: Fishing-themed collectibles with no special ability. Each one has a hidden Luck of the Sea I enchant and otherwise works like its base item. For example, the Fishers Boots are ordinary leather boots and the Guardian Glaive is an ordinary trident.

details.text: They all share one simple template: the base item, a name, a line of lore, hidden Luck of the Sea I, and the Collectible tier. The code gives them no abilities.
The Lost Lantern and Aqua Lotus can't be placed as blocks. The plugin blocks placing any of its custom items.

pride-2025-tokens.summary: Pride 2025 event tokens with no ability of their own. The Maze Token marks that you finished the Pride 2025 maze. The Pride Token is the event's currency, and whatever it buys is handled somewhere else, not in the item's code.

details.text: Both have a hidden Unbreaking I enchant and no special behaviour in the code.

radiant-charm.summary: Hold it in either hand to get 10 seconds of hidden Regeneration II about every 31.5 seconds. The tooltip doesn't mention this.

numbers.label: Effect
numbers.value: Regeneration II for 10 s (200 ticks)

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 30 s (600 ticks)

numbers.label: Real gap
numbers.value: About 31.5 s while you keep holding it. The check only runs every 3.5 s (70 ticks), and the 9th check is the first one after the 30 s cooldown ends.

details.text: It only works in your main hand or off-hand. The periodic check looks at your worn armor and both hands, not the rest of your inventory.
The effect shows no particles and no effect icon.

pride-shard-lantern.summary: Hold it in either hand for constant hidden Night Vision. It can't be placed as a block.

numbers.label: Night Vision
numbers.value: 15 s (300 ticks), reapplied every 3.5 s (70 ticks) while held

details.text: Night Vision lasts up to 15 seconds after you stop holding it. It shows no particles or icon.
It works in your main hand or off-hand, not from elsewhere in your inventory.
Placing it is blocked.

st-patricks-helmet.summary: A collectible turtle shell with no special ability and no extra enchantments. It works like a normal turtle shell.

details.text: The item only sets a name, lore and a Collectible tier. There is no ability code.

mini-poppy.summary: Holding this poppy in either hand, or wearing it on your head, shrinks you to half size. It can't be placed or composted.

use.text: Right-click while holding it in your main hand to wear it on your head. This only works if your helmet slot is empty.

numbers.label: Size
numbers.value: −0.5 scale (normal is 1.0, so half size) in your main hand, off-hand or head slot

details.text: Placing it and putting it in a composter are both blocked.
Hard-disabled in the event_new world. There you can't move it into your hotbar or armor slots or scroll to it.

easter-charm.summary: A reward for completing Explorer Miles. The tooltip hints it might do something if you keep it, but the code gives it no ability. It's a rabbit's foot with Knockback IV and Unbreaking X.

details.text: The item only sets a name, lore and enchants. There is no ability code.

valentide-charms.summary: The three Valentide 2025 team charms (HeartBreakers, Rosethorn and Sweethearts) have no ability. Like the other charms, each has Knockback IV and Unbreaking X.

details.text: A comment in the code says the author may add functionality to these charms "someday". For now there is none.
All three charms are the same item underneath. Only the name and a stored team tag tell them apart.

beloved-fallow.summary: A netherite hoe that puts nearby adult animals into love mode on right-click, the same as feeding them, so they breed without food.

use.text: Right-click while holding it (either hand). Every animal around you that can breed right now gets hearts and goes into love mode.

numbers.label: Area
numbers.value: 5 blocks in every direction from you (a 10×10×10 box centred on you)

numbers.label: Love mode
numbers.value: 30 s (600 ticks)

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 2 min (2400 ticks)

details.text: Animals the game says can't breed right now are skipped.
The cooldown only starts if at least one animal was affected. While on cooldown, right-clicking does nothing and shows no message.
Claims and regions aren't checked. It works on any animals in range, including other players' animals.

quirks.text: The tooltip says "5x5", but the search reaches 5 blocks out in every direction, so it covers a 10×10 area centred on you (and 5 blocks up and down).

config.text: Which animals count as able to breed is decided by the game. That should mean adults that aren't on a breeding cooldown, so babies are skipped. This depends on the game, not tested.

blooming-bunny-rake.summary: A netherite hoe with a "crop of the day". When you break that crop with it, there's a 15% chance the drops are doubled.

use.text: Break the day's crop with the rake in your main hand.
Switching hotbar slots while holding the rake shows the crop of the day in your action bar.

numbers.label: Bonus chance
numbers.value: 15% per crop block broken

numbers.label: Crop by day of month
numbers.value: 1, 8, 15, 22, 29: Potatoes · 2, 9, 16, 23, 30: Carrots · 3, 10, 17, 24, 31: Wheat · 4, 11, 18, 25: Beetroots · 5, 12, 19, 26: Nether Wart · 6, 13, 20, 27: Sugar Cane · 7, 14, 21, 28: Mushrooms (red and brown)

details.text: When the bonus triggers, the drops are worked out again for the rake in your hand and then doubled. If the block drops one or two stacks, all of them are doubled. With more stacks, only the first half (rounded down) plus one are doubled.
Crop growth isn't checked, so unripe crops can trigger it too. The bonus just doubles whatever they would drop.

quirks.text: The crop of the day is picked from the server's date once, when the plugin starts up, not at midnight. It only changes after a restart, so it can be out of date on a server that has been running for more than a day.
The action-bar message also shows on every scroll while the rake is in your off-hand.

config.text: The scroll check looks at what you're holding at the moment you scroll. The game most likely runs it before the switch happens, which would mean the message shows when you scroll away from the rake rather than onto it. This depends on the game, not tested.

heartstring-hatchet.summary: A netherite axe that gives extra reach while it's in your main hand. Sneak and right-click to start a vacuum that swirls nearby dropped items toward you for about 25 seconds.

use.text: Sneak and right-click (hatchet in either hand) to start the vacuum.

numbers.label: Extra reach
numbers.value: +4.5 blocks for both blocks and entities, in the main hand only

numbers.label: Vacuum cooldown
numbers.value: 40 s (800 ticks)

numbers.label: Vacuum area
numbers.value: 10 blocks in every direction, moving with you

numbers.label: Vacuum duration
numbers.value: About 25 s (one push every 5 ticks, 102 pushes)

details.text: Items are pushed toward your eyes with a sideways twist, so they swirl around you rather than flying straight in.
It pulls every dropped item in range.
The cooldown starts even if there were no items nearby.
Hard-disabled in the pinata world. There you can't move it into your hotbar or armor slots or scroll to it.

quirks.text: To decide whether an item still needs pushing, the code adds the three distance offsets (x, y, z) together instead of measuring the real distance. So an item can stop being pulled while it's still far from you, if its offsets happen to cancel out.
On the last round the code tries to stop every item in range, but then gives them one more push straight away, so items don't actually stop when the vacuum ends.

spring-hatchet.summary: A netherite axe with Silk Touch that breaks any glass instantly when you left-click it.

use.text: Left-click glass with the hatchet in your main hand. This covers glass, tinted glass, all stained glass, glass panes and stained glass panes.

config.text: The glass is broken as if you had mined it yourself with the hatchet. That should mean its Silk Touch lets you keep the glass and claim or region protection still applies. This depends on the game and the server's protection plugins, not tested.

ballistic-bunny-nouveau.summary: A netherite pickaxe that charges up as you mine. Each block you break adds one charge. Press your swap-hands key (F) to set off an explosion where you stand, and the more you've mined, the bigger it is.

use.text: Break blocks with it in your main hand to build charge.
Press F with it in either hand to explode. The blast goes off 0.25 s later at your position, with no fire.

numbers.label: Minimum charge
numbers.value: 100 blocks (explosion power 4, the same as TNT)

numbers.label: Max power
numbers.value: 40, reached at about 23,700 blocks

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 1 min (1200 ticks)

numbers.label: Delay
numbers.value: 0.25 s (5 ticks) from pressing F to the blast

details.text: Charge belongs to you, not to the pickaxe, so it carries over to any copy you use. It isn't saved and is lost when the server restarts.
A successful explosion resets your charge to 0. If you press F while it's on cooldown or below 100 charge, you get an action-bar message and keep your charge.
Pressing F with it in either hand never swaps your hands.

quirks.text: Charge stops at 32,767. The next block you break after that sets off a max-power (40) blast on its own, even during the cooldown, and resets your charge to 0.

config.text: The item itself doesn't check claims or regions before exploding. Whether the blast breaks blocks in a given place depends on the game and the server's protection and explosion settings, not tested.

peep-plushy-mattock.summary: A netherite pickaxe (Fortune VI) that gambles on ores. Each ore you mine has an 18% chance to drop 7 times as much, a 7% chance to drop nothing, and otherwise drops normally.

numbers.label: 7× drops
numbers.value: 18% per ore

numbers.label: No drops
numbers.value: 7% per ore

numbers.label: Normal drops
numbers.value: 75% per ore

details.text: It counts every coal, copper, iron, gold, redstone, emerald, lapis and diamond ore (deepslate versions and nether gold ore included) plus nether quartz ore. Ancient debris doesn't count.
On a 7× roll, the drops are worked out for the pickaxe in your hand, then multiplied by 7. Only item drops change. XP is untouched.
It must be in your main hand. The ability is off in the event_new world.

quirks.text: On a 7× roll, the first kind of drop is repeated once for each stack the ore would drop. If an ore ever dropped two different items, you'd get two helpings of the first one and none of the second.

twin-flame-pickaxe.summary: A netherite pickaxe that switches between Fortune V and Silk Touch when you press your swap-hands key (F).

use.text: Press F with it in your main hand. It switches between Fortune V and Silk Touch, and the action bar shows which one is active.

details.text: It starts with Fortune V.
It only works in your main hand. If it's in your off-hand, F swaps your hands as normal.

splitsoul-multi-tool.summary: Right-click the SplitSoul Bag to get a SplitSoul Multi-Tool with a random personality. The Multi-Tool becomes whichever tool mines a block fastest when you left-click it, turns into a sword when you hit something, and switches between Silk Touch and Fortune with F. Very rarely, its personality acts up.

use.text: Bag: hold it in your main hand and right-click to use it up and receive a Multi-Tool.
Left-click a block with the Multi-Tool in your main hand. It becomes whichever of netherite pickaxe, shovel, axe, hoe, shears or sword breaks that block fastest.
Hit a mob with it in your main hand and it becomes a netherite sword.
Press F with it in your main hand to switch between Silk Touch I and Fortune IV. It starts with Silk Touch.

numbers.label: Personality
numbers.value: Pleasant, Lazy, Sad or Upset, 25% each, fixed on each tool

numbers.label: Mood event
numbers.value: 1 in 25,000 per block left-click or hit

numbers.label: Random chatter
numbers.value: 1 in 9,000 per block left-click or hit (only talk)

numbers.label: Refusal length
numbers.value: 5 minutes

details.text: A mood event is one of four, picked at random. Each starts with lines of dialogue in the tool's voice.
Refuse to work: for 5 minutes, every block left-click and hit with it is cancelled, with a message telling you to give it some space.
Effects, all lasting 60 s. Upset gives Darkness. Sad gives Nausea and Slowness III. Lazy gives Slowness XXI. Pleasant gives Haste III and Speed III instead.
Teleport. Lazy moves you 1 to 29 blocks along each axis and Upset 1 to 99 blocks, always east, up and south. There's no check on where you land. Pleasant and Sad only talk.

Explosion at your feet. Lazy and Sad make a power 4 blast (TNT strength) and Upset a power 10 blast. Pleasant only talks. The blast only breaks blocks and starts fires if you're allowed to build where you're standing.
When it turns into shears, it gets netherite-level durability (2031).

quirks.text: The 5-minute refusal is tied to you, not to the tool, so switching to another Multi-Tool doesn't get around it. The tool still changes shape during the refusal. Only your click is cancelled.

hearthook-lure.summary: An unbreakable fishing rod with Lure VI. Casts fly out faster. Hooking a mob and reeling in pulls the mob straight to you, or pulls you to the mob if you're sneaking.

use.text: Hook a living mob and reel in. The mob is teleported to you. Sneak while reeling in to teleport yourself to the mob instead.

numbers.label: Cast speed
numbers.value: 1.8× normal

details.text: The pull doesn't work on mobs you aren't allowed to damage (WorldGuard or Towny). Players count as mobs here, so it also works on players where you're allowed to hurt them.
The rod works in either hand. On a successful pull, the hook is removed and the normal reel-in is cancelled.

quirks.text: If you hold another custom item in your other hand, only one of the two items' fishing abilities runs (whichever the plugin checks first). The lure's pull may not trigger.

config.text: When you cast, the rod switches off the game's sky check for the hook, which should mean bite times aren't slowed when the hook can't see the sky. This depends on the game, not tested.

prismatic-pruners.summary: Shears that get 1 to 2 white wool from almost any mob you right-click, once per mob.

use.text: Right-click a mob while holding the shears in either hand.

numbers.label: Wool
numbers.value: 1 to 2 white wool per mob

numbers.label: Limit
numbers.value: Once per mob, ever (the mob is marked after shearing)

details.text: Sheep and players are skipped. Any other living mob works, including armor stands.
It doesn't hurt the mob and has no cooldown. Claims aren't checked.

config.text: The right-click isn't cancelled, so the mob's normal right-click action (such as a villager's trade window) should still happen too. This depends on the game, not tested.

rainbow-shears.summary: Shears that add 1 to 4 extra wool blocks in random colours every time they shear something.

numbers.label: Bonus wool
numbers.value: 1 to 4 blocks per shear, each one of the 16 colours at random

details.text: Players have to hold them in the main hand.
It also works when a dispenser holding the shears does the shearing.
The mob type isn't checked, so anything the shears can shear gets the bonus wool, not just sheep.

hare-howitzer.summary: A bow that fires a rabbit instead of an arrow. The rabbit explodes as soon as anything other than air is right beside it (a wall, a plant, water).

numbers.label: Fire rate
numbers.value: 1 shot per second (20 ticks). Shots during the cooldown are cancelled.

numbers.label: Explosion
numbers.value: Power 2.4, with no fire and no block damage

details.text: The rabbit flies with the arrow's speed and direction. Every tick it checks the blocks directly north, south, east and west of it, and explodes if any of them isn't air. The block underneath doesn't count, so landing on open flat ground doesn't set it off by itself.
The rabbit drops nothing and gives no XP.

quirks.text: The "no drops, no XP" rule also applies to every mob you kill while holding the bow in either hand, including melee kills with the bow in your off-hand. Those mobs drop nothing and give no XP.
The rabbit starts where the arrow would. If you shoot while standing right against a wall, it can blow up immediately in front of you.

config.text: The rabbit is launched as if it had already fallen 100 blocks, so it should die when it lands. The code also tries to explode a rabbit that has died, but it stops watching any rabbit the game no longer counts as valid first, so a rabbit that dies this way most likely vanishes without exploding. This depends on the game, not tested.

strasz-bows.summary: A bow (Longbow) and a crossbow (Arcbow) with the same ability. Your shots become fast red bolts that fly straight. A hit deals heavy damage that grows with the target's health, and the first hit fires copies at up to 21 nearby mobs.

numbers.label: Bolt speed
numbers.value: 1.5× the arrow's speed, with no drop for 5.5 s (110 ticks)

numbers.label: Hit damage
numbers.value: 10 + 10% of the target's current health

numbers.label: Copies
numbers.value: Up to 21, one per mob within 20 blocks (in each direction) of the one you hit

details.text: Copies are fired once in a straight line from the hit mob toward each other mob it can see. They don't steer, and gravity pulls them down. They deal the same damage but don't make more copies.
Endermen take no damage from it.
The damage is always the formula above. Draw strength and the Power enchant don't change it, because the arrow is replaced.
The ability is off in the pinata world.

quirks.text: Every projectile you launch while holding either bow in either hand is swapped for a red bolt, not just arrows from the bow. That includes things thrown from your other hand.
Copies target every living thing except players, including your pets, villagers, iron golems and armor stands.

rosethorn-rapier.summary: A netherite sword. Right-click any entity to draw a magic circle where you're standing. For 10 seconds, mobs you kill inside it drop bigger stacks.

use.text: Right-click any entity with the rapier in either hand. The circle stays where you were standing.

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 35 s (700 ticks)

numbers.label: Circle
numbers.value: 5-block radius around where you stood

numbers.label: Duration
numbers.value: 10 s (200 ticks)

numbers.label: Loot bonus
numbers.value: Each drop stack gains 1/3 of its size (rounded down). This becomes 1/2 once the circle's kill tally passes 130.

details.text: The kill tally adds each killed mob's max health (a zombie adds 20) until it reaches 200. Each new circle starts again at 0.
The kill has to be yours, the mob has to die inside the circle, and the rapier has to be in your hand when it dies. XP isn't changed.

quirks.text: Because the bonus is rounded down, a drop of a single item never increases. A stack of 2 only gains in the second tier. A line that would have added +1 to every stack is switched off in the code.

yolkplaid-yataghan.summary: A netherite sword. Right-click while looking at a mob up to 35 blocks away to trap it in a giant egg for 12 seconds. The trapped mob can't move or act, glows, and takes 4 damage every second.

use.text: Look at a mob and right-click with the sword in either hand.

numbers.label: Range
numbers.value: 35 blocks

numbers.label: Charges
numbers.value: 2 eggs at a time. Each recharges 20 s (400 ticks) after it's used.

numbers.label: Trap time
numbers.value: 12 s (240 ticks)

numbers.label: Damage
numbers.value: 4 per second, 13 hits in all (52 before armor)

details.text: Players can't be targeted, and neither can mobs you aren't allowed to damage (WorldGuard or Towny).
While trapped, the mob can't act on its own and glows in a random colour. The damage counts as yours. The egg disappears early if the mob dies.
When both eggs are recharging, right-clicking does nothing and shows no message.

quirks.text: There's code meant to stop trapped mobs from teleporting, but it never runs, because trapped mobs are never marked for it.

dazzling-hearts-scythe.summary: A netherite hoe. Right-click to strike the mob you're looking at, or a spot in front of you, with 7 rapid waves of slashes over about 2 seconds. The first wave also slows targets heavily.

use.text: Right-click with it in your main hand. It aims at the mob you're looking at (up to 50 blocks), otherwise the block you're looking at (up to 10 blocks), otherwise a point 10 blocks ahead.

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 8 s (160 ticks)

numbers.label: Hit area
numbers.value: 2 blocks to each side and 2.5 blocks up and down from the target point

numbers.label: Damage
numbers.value: 14 per wave, 7 waves: one right away, then one every 0.35 s (7 ticks)

numbers.label: Slow
numbers.value: Slowness IV for 2.8 s (56 ticks), first wave only

details.text: The first wave also cancels the targets' current momentum.
It hits every living thing in the area except you. The ability itself doesn't check claims or regions.
The ability is off in the pinata world.

quirks.text: Once a mob is caught, every later wave hits it, even if it has left the area. Each wave also adds the mobs it finds to the list again, so the code damages a mob that stays in the area more than once in the same wave.

config.text: Whether hits on other players or pets actually land depends on the server's PvP and protection rules.

Waves come every 0.35 s, which is faster than the game's usual short hit immunity after a mob is hurt, and repeat hits in the same wave land at the same moment. So some of those hits may deal less or nothing. This depends on the game, not tested.

springtide-scythe.summary: A netherite hoe whose right-click changes with the time of day. By day, Downpour slows everything around the target and rains stars on it for about 7.5 seconds. By night, Starcrossers sends two homing stars that burst on impact.

use.text: Right-click with it in either hand. By day it aims at the mob you're looking at, or the top of the block you're looking at. By night it aims at the entity or block you're looking at. The range is 45 blocks in both cases.

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 8 s (160 ticks), shared by both modes

numbers.label: Downpour slow
numbers.value: Slowness III for 7.5 s (150 ticks) on everything within 3 blocks of the target

numbers.label: Downpour stars
numbers.value: About 151 stars over about 7.5 s, falling from 9 to 11 blocks up, within 3 blocks of the target

numbers.label: Downpour damage
numbers.value: 20 per direct hit. A star that lands on a block deals 10 to a mob right next to that block.

numbers.label: Starcrossers stars
numbers.value: 2 stars that start 10 blocks above you (up to 8 blocks to the side), fly at 1 block per tick and steer for about 4 s (81 ticks)

numbers.label: Starcrossers damage
numbers.value: 25 to the first mob within 3 blocks of the impact, then 1 less for each mob after it

details.text: Star damage skips you and mobs you aren't allowed to damage (WorldGuard or Towny). Downpour's slow only skips you, not protected mobs.
Day or night is decided by the game's own daytime check for your world.
The ability is off in the pinata world.

quirks.text: Starcrossers stops dealing damage as soon as it reaches you or a protected mob in its list of nearby mobs. Anything checked after that takes nothing, so standing near your own impact can cancel some or all of the damage.
When Starcrossers is aimed at a mob, the stars only steer while both are still flying. Once one lands, the other stops steering and flies on without aiming.

config.text: Downpour drops a star every 0.05 s, faster than the game's usual short hit immunity after a mob is hurt, so a mob hit by several stars in quick succession may not take the full damage from each. This depends on the game, not tested.

bubble-board-boots.summary: Boots that let you walk up single blocks, jump a bit higher, and launch yourself high into the air by holding sneak on the ground and then letting go.

use.text: Stand on the ground and hold sneak. After 1 second bubbles start popping at your feet; at 1.75 seconds a bell chimes. Let go of sneak after the chime to launch.
The launch throws you strongly upward and a little in the direction you're looking.

numbers.label: Charge time
numbers.value: 1.75 s of sneaking (35 ticks); bubbles show from 1 s

numbers.label: Launch speed
numbers.value: 2.5 straight up, plus 1.5× the level (sideways) part of your look direction

numbers.label: Step height
numbers.value: +1 block while worn

numbers.label: Jump strength
numbers.value: +0.2 while worn

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: None

details.text: The charge is lost if you leave the ground, or if you let go of sneak before the chime. Nothing happens then; just try again.

quirks.text: The sneak launch doesn't check that the boots are on your feet. Holding them in your main hand or off-hand works too. The step-height and jump bonuses only count while they're worn.

hellstriders.summary: Frost Walker for lava: walking at the edge of a lava pool turns the still lava around you into temporary obsidian, which slowly crumbles back into lava.

use.text: Walk while standing on a solid block that has lava next to it. Each time you step onto a new block, still lava within 3 blocks at that level becomes obsidian, as long as the space above it is empty.

numbers.label: Freeze radius
numbers.value: 3 blocks around the block under you

numbers.label: Decay check
numbers.value: Every 1.5 s (30 ticks)

numbers.label: Leash
numbers.value: Obsidian picked in a decay check that is more than 10 blocks from you (or in another world) turns straight back to lava

details.text: Only still lava (source blocks) freezes. Flowing lava doesn't, and neither does lava with a block on top of it. It won't start while you're flying or while you're swimming in lava with nothing solid under you.

The obsidian decays over time: obsidian turns into crying obsidian, then back into lava. Each check moves up to 18 randomly picked blocks one step along, and once 40 or more of these blocks exist, a quarter of them also move a step every check.
If you try to mine the obsidian, the break is cancelled and the block turns straight back into lava.
All of your obsidian turns back into lava at once when you take the boots off your feet, teleport, or log out.
It works in every world; no world switches it off.

quirks.text: The lava-freezing doesn't check that the boots are on your feet, so it also happens while you hold them in either hand.

tropicleaf-gliders.summary: An elytra that cuts 15% off every hit of damage you take while it's in your chest slot, whether or not you're flying.

numbers.label: Damage reduction
numbers.value: 15% of each hit

numbers.label: Durability cost
numbers.value: 1 durability point on the elytra each time you take damage

details.text: It has to be worn in the chest slot. Holding it does nothing.
It applies to every kind of damage (falls, fire, mobs, and so on), not only damage taken while gliding.

neptunes-crown.summary: A wearable crown (an amethyst cluster) that gives Water Breathing while you're in water and keeps clearing Mining Fatigue off you the whole time you wear it.

use.text: Right-click it in your main hand to put it on, if your helmet slot is empty. You can also click it into the helmet slot in your inventory. Right-clicking with it never places the cluster as a block.

numbers.label: Water Breathing
numbers.value: 15 s (300 ticks), re-applied every 3.5 s while you're in water

numbers.label: Mining Fatigue clear
numbers.value: Every 3.5 s (70 ticks)

details.text: Mining Fatigue is removed whenever you wear the crown, in or out of water, not only while submerged as the tooltip suggests. That includes the curse from Elder Guardians.
The removal runs every 3.5 seconds, so a fresh dose of Mining Fatigue can stay on you for up to that long before it's cleared.
Both effects need the crown in your head slot. Holding it does nothing.

sunbrellahat.summary: A helmet with three abilities: sneak while falling to glide down slowly, sprint-hits that knock enemies much further, and arrows that turn into invisible, gravity-free wind slashes.

use.text: Tailwind: while falling, hold sneak. Your fall slows, you drift in the direction you're looking, and your fall distance keeps being reset.
Trailblazer: hit something while sprinting (not a critical hit) and it gets launched away from you.
WindTye: any arrow you fire flies in a straight line with no gravity, shown only as sweep and cloud particles.

numbers.label: Glide fall speed
numbers.value: Downward speed halved on every movement step

numbers.label: Glide drift
numbers.value: 0.25× your look direction

numbers.label: Glide fall distance
numbers.value: Reset to 0.5 blocks on every step

numbers.label: Trailblazer launch
numbers.value: 1.5× the distance between you and the target, plus a small lift, capped at 3 per direction

numbers.label: Wind slash lifetime
numbers.value: About 6.6 s (133 ticks), then the arrow is removed

details.text: The glide switches off when there's a non-air block (including water) within 2 blocks below you, so the last couple of blocks are a normal fall.
The Trailblazer push scales with how far the target is from you, so targets hit from further away get launched harder, up to the cap.
Wind-slash arrows are hidden from you and from every player within 100 blocks when fired. They're removed the moment they hit anything and aren't saved with the world, so you can't pick them back up.
Only normal and tipped arrows count; other projectiles (tridents, snowballs, spectral arrows) aren't changed. This includes arrows from crossbows.

quirks.text: None of the three abilities checks that the hat is on your head. Holding it in either hand gives you the glide, the sprint-hit launch and the wind-slash arrows too.
Trailblazer also fires when one of your arrows or other projectiles hits something while you happen to be sprinting.

crimson-rune.summary: Hold it in either hand to keep Fire Resistance on you.

numbers.label: Fire Resistance
numbers.value: 12.5 s (250 ticks), re-applied every 3.5 s while held

details.text: It works from your main hand or off-hand. Anywhere else in your inventory it does nothing.
The effect has no particles but shows its icon. It stays on for up to 12.5 seconds after you stop holding the rune.

hearty-shroom.summary: Hold it in either hand for 2 extra hearts of max health. It can't be placed as a mushroom.

numbers.label: Max health
numbers.value: +4 (2 hearts) while held

details.text: Trying to place it is always cancelled, so it can't be planted by accident.

infinite-buckets.summary: Buckets that place water or lava without ever emptying. They respect claims and copy most normal bucket behaviour.

use.text: Empty the bucket as usual, from your main hand or off-hand. The fluid is placed and the bucket stays full.

details.text: Nothing is placed where you aren't allowed to build (claims and regions are respected).
The water bucket fills waterloggable blocks (slabs, stairs and so on). In dimensions where water evaporates, like the Nether, it just fizzles.
Replaceable blocks like grass or flowers are broken (and drop) to make room for the fluid. Anything else blocks the placement.
Block changes are logged to the server's block-logging plugins under your name.

quirks.text: The Infinite Water Bucket can't scoop up fish or axolotls. Trying is simply cancelled.

config.text: The plugin has code for filling cauldrons (a full water cauldron, or a lava cauldron unless water is directly above it), but whether using the bucket on a cauldron actually reaches that code depends on the server software. Test it before relying on it.

sweet-summer-honey.summary: Hold it for Haste I and Speed I. Drink it for a big Absorption boost every 7 minutes, and the bottle is never used up.

use.text: Hold it in your main hand or off-hand for Haste I and Speed I.
Drink it for Absorption IV. You keep the bottle.

numbers.label: Haste I + Speed I
numbers.value: 17.5 s (350 ticks), re-applied every 3.5 s while held

numbers.label: Absorption
numbers.value: Level IV (8 extra hearts) for 60 s (1200 ticks)

numbers.label: Drink cooldown
numbers.value: 7 min (8400 ticks)

details.text: Drinking it during the cooldown does nothing and shows no message.

quirks.text: While the honey is in either hand, you can't eat or drink anything else. The honey cancels every food or drink you finish, and if it's off cooldown it gives its Absorption instead. Keep it out of your off-hand when you need to eat.
Its Haste turns off the Big Swing Pickaxe's wide swing: that pickaxe strips Haste and refuses to area-mine while you have it.

lumalympics-charm.summary: A participation keepsake from the Lumalympics. Despite the teasing lore, the plugin gives it no ability at all; nothing else in the code refers to it.

details.text: The item class defines only its name, lore and enchant (Unbreaking X), with no ability hooks.

config.text: If the charm ever does something (for example, it gets checked by another plugin or a later event), that logic isn't in LumaItems at this commit.

bobble-blower.summary: Swing it at full charge to lob three slow bubbles that bounce along the ground, knocking out any crops they pass over with Fortune V drops.

use.text: Left-click (swing at the air or a block) when your swing is fully charged. It fires 3 bubbles: one straight ahead and one 6° to each side.

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 5 s (100 ticks)

numbers.label: Spread
numbers.value: 3 bubbles, ±6°

numbers.label: Throw speed
numbers.value: 35% of a normal snowball throw

numbers.label: Bounce
numbers.value: Keeps 85% of its speed per bounce; stops when slower than 0.2, more than 20 blocks from you, or in liquid

numbers.label: Crop reach
numbers.value: Up to about 6 blocks below each bubble (the check starts 1 block above it and looks 7 down), every 0.1 s

numbers.label: Durability
numbers.value: 1 per crop broken

details.text: Crops are broken as if by a Fortune V netherite hoe, so they drop extra.
Growth stage isn't checked. Unripe crops are broken too. 'Crops' means the game's crop list plus nether wart.
Crops in claims where you can't build are left alone.
Swinging before the charge bar is full does nothing and doesn't start the cooldown.

quirks.text: It also fires from the off-hand: with the hoe in your off-hand, any fully charged left-click lobs bubbles. Watch out: the durability for broken crops is always taken from whatever is in your main hand, not from the hoe.

big-swing-pickaxe.summary: A Silk Touch pickaxe that breaks a wide oval of blocks around every block you mine and gives you 2 extra blocks of reach, but mines much more slowly.

use.text: Mine a block with it in your main hand. Every solid block in an oval around it breaks too, wider to your sides than in front and behind.

numbers.label: Area
numbers.value: Oval about 4 blocks to each side, 2.5 forward/back, 2 up/down from the mined block

numbers.label: Mining speed
numbers.value: −0.75 block break speed

numbers.label: Reach
numbers.value: +2 blocks for blocks and for hitting mobs (main hand only)

details.text: The extra blocks drop as if mined by this pickaxe, so Silk Touch applies. They don't cost extra durability.
It skips container and utility blocks (chests, barrels, shulker boxes, furnaces, hoppers, spawners, signs, farmland, bedrock and similar) and anything non-solid.
It can't be combined with Haste. If you have Haste when you mine, the Haste effect is removed, the wide swing is skipped, and you get a 'Cannot be used with Haste.' message.
It's switched off in the piñata world, where you can't even equip it.

quirks.text: The mining-speed and attack-speed penalties apply in any hand, including the off-hand, even though the wide swing and reach only work from the main hand.

config.text: How slow −0.75 break speed feels depends on your base mining speed, which the game sets, not this plugin. On a default server the base is 1, which would leave about a quarter of normal speed.

The wide swing is skipped when the game reports an unlimited break speed for the block you mined. That should mean blocks with no hardness at all (flowers, torches and the like), not blocks you mine instantly thanks to Efficiency. Not tested in game.

blobble-hammer.summary: A Fortune V pickaxe. Mining an ore sprays out bouncing coloured bubbles, and each block a bubble touches is broken with Fortune V drops.

use.text: Mine an ore (coal, iron, copper, gold incl. nether gold, redstone, emerald, lapis, diamond, or nether quartz) with it in your main hand. Bubbles spray out from the ore.

numbers.label: Bubbles per ore
numbers.value: Half of a Fortune V drop roll, rounded down, max 5 per drop type

numbers.label: Bubble lifetime
numbers.value: About 1.5 s (30 ticks) of bouncing, or until more than 20 blocks from you

numbers.label: Durability
