numbers.value: 1 per block a bubble breaks

details.text: Blocks hit by bubbles break as if mined by a Fortune V netherite pickaxe and drop experience. Ores caught by a bubble get Fortune V drops too.
Bubbles only break blocks a pickaxe is the right tool for. They skip containers and other protected blocks, and anything in a claim where you can't build.
Blocks broken by bubbles don't spawn more bubbles.
Ancient debris isn't counted as an ore.

quirks.text: The bubble count comes from its own separate Fortune V roll, halved and rounded down. So when an ore rolls a single item (common for diamond, emerald, coal or quartz), no bubbles come out.
Bubble durability is taken from whatever is in your main hand when the bubble lands, even if you've switched away from the hammer.

seaside-surf-rod.summary: A fishing rod that sometimes gambles your catch. A win turns it into 2–3 of the item with double XP; a loss deletes it. Your odds improve with your lifetime fish-caught stat.

use.text: Fish normally, with the rod in either hand. Each catch has a small chance to become a wager.

numbers.label: Chance a catch is wagered
numbers.value: 11 in 101 (~10.9%), +1 per 1,000 fish caught, capped at 16 in 101 (~15.8%)

numbers.label: Chance a wager wins
numbers.value: 71 in 101 (~70.3%), +1 per 1,000 fish caught, no cap

numbers.label: Win
numbers.value: Catch becomes 2 or 3 of the item; XP doubled

numbers.label: Loss
numbers.value: The caught item is deleted

details.text: 'Fish caught' is your vanilla Fish Caught statistic, counted in whole thousands.
A win only changes items that stack. For unstackable catches (enchanted books, bows, rods and the like) you get the win effects but the item and XP stay as they were.
A loss only removes the item; the catch's XP is untouched. Purple and light-blue particles with a firework sound mean a win; red particles with a witch laugh mean a loss.

quirks.text: The wager chance is capped at 5,000 fish caught, but the win chance keeps rising. At 30,000 fish caught every wager wins.

hailstorm-shovel.summary: Right-click to lob a seed that grows into a drifting storm cloud. For about 10 seconds it rains hail that digs up shovel blocks with Silk Touch, pushes the drops toward you, and hurts mobs.

use.text: Right-click while standing somewhere the sky light reaches. A slow seed is thrown; where it lands, a column of cloud rises 11 blocks, and then the storm starts about 10 blocks above the landing spot.

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 3 min (3600 ticks), starting when you throw

numbers.label: Storm length
numbers.value: About 10 s (201 hailstones, one per tick)

numbers.label: Storm area
numbers.value: Hail falls anywhere in a 12×12 square centred on the cloud (up to 6 blocks out each way)

numbers.label: Cloud drift
numbers.value: Up to 0.1 blocks per tick (about 20 blocks over the whole storm) in the direction you face when the storm starts; looking up or down makes it drift slower and off to one side

numbers.label: Hail damage
numbers.value: 5 (2.5 hearts) per hailstone to mobs

details.text: It won't fire when no sky light reaches your feet (for example deep underground or in a closed room). The cooldown isn't used up then.
Any right-click counts, including opening a door or chest while holding the shovel, so it's easy to launch a storm by accident.

Hail breaks blocks a shovel is the right tool for (dirt, sand, gravel, snow and so on) as if mined with a Silk Touch shovel. It skips protected blocks like farmland and paths, and anything in a claim where you can't build. It costs the shovel no durability.
Items dropped near a broken block are flung toward you.
Hail passes harmlessly through players, and mobs you aren't allowed to hurt are skipped.

quirks.text: It also fires from the off-hand: with the shovel in your off-hand, right-clicking with anything, even placing a block, launches a storm.
The code tries to move the storm to the surface when the seed lands in water, but that step does nothing. The storm always forms from where the seed landed.

config.text: Whether a world has sky light at all is a world setting, not part of this plugin. On a default server the Nether and the End have none, so the shovel likely can't be used there.

trishear-rigger.summary: A bow that fires three arrows at once. They spread sideways on the ground and up/down in the air, and on a full draw each arrow that hits a block explodes a second later.

use.text: Shoot normally. On the ground (or while hovering in flight) the two extra arrows spread left and right; while jumping or falling they spread up and down.
Draw to at least 80% power and every arrow that sticks into a block glows, then explodes 1 second later.

numbers.label: Spread
numbers.value: ±5° from the centre arrow

numbers.label: Explosion draw
numbers.value: At least 80% draw

numbers.label: Explosion delay
numbers.value: 1 s (20 ticks) after hitting a block

numbers.label: Explosion reach
numbers.value: Living things within about 2.5 blocks of the arrow

numbers.label: Explosion damage
numbers.value: 6 minus the target's distance from the arrow in blocks (6 right on top of it, less further out)

details.text: When an arrow hits a mob, the mob's short hit-immunity is reset, so all three arrows can land on the same target.
Only arrows that hit a block explode. An arrow that hits a mob doesn't. The blast never hurts you.
The two extra arrows don't use up ammo and can't be picked up. They copy the centre arrow's speed, Piercing level and colour.

quirks.text: Arrows from this bow never crit. The centre arrow's critical flag is switched off before the copies are made, so a full draw doesn't give the usual bonus damage.

config.text: The explosion counts as damage dealt by you, so the server's usual PvP and protection rules decide whether it can hurt other players or their animals.

heavy-blob-wand.summary: A Sharpness X sword that fires a stream of bouncing bubbles when you swing. A full-charge swing fires 4, and each bubble deals a flat 13 damage.

use.text: Left-click (swing at the air or a block). The more charged your swing, the more bubbles: one every 0.1 s, fired wherever you're looking at that moment.

numbers.label: Damage
numbers.value: 13 (6.5 hearts) per bubble, before armor

numbers.label: Bounce
numbers.value: Keeps 88% of its speed; stops when slower than 0.3 or more than 20 blocks from you

numbers.label: Durability
numbers.value: 1 per bubble that hits a mob

details.text: A bubble that hits a mob cancels its knockback (the target stops dead) and resets its hit-immunity, so a full stream can land every bubble.
Bubble damage is a flat 13; Sharpness and critical hits don't change it. It skips anything you aren't allowed to hurt.
Swinging below 45% charge fires nothing. There's no cooldown beyond the swing charge.

quirks.text: It also fires from the off-hand: with the wand there, left-clicking with anything lobs bubbles based on your main-hand swing charge. Durability is taken from whatever is in your main hand when a bubble lands.

heavy-prism-sickle.summary: The Heavy Prism Core opens into a Heavy Prism Sickle with a random colour theme. The sickle summons six orbs behind your head that fire sweeping beams at nearby mobs or at a target you lock on to.

use.text: Core: right-click while holding it. The core is used up and a Heavy Prism Sickle goes into your inventory.
Sickle: right-click with it in your main hand. Look straight at a mob first to lock all orbs onto it; otherwise the orbs pick their own targets.

numbers.label: Lock-on range
numbers.value: 25 blocks

numbers.label: Firing delay
numbers.value: Locked on: all orbs after 0.75 s. Otherwise in pairs at 2.5 s, 3.25 s and 4 s

numbers.label: Auto-target range
numbers.value: 20 blocks from each orb, nearest to you first, max 2 orbs per target

numbers.label: Beam damage
numbers.value: 8 per hit; passes through up to 8 targets in a line

numbers.label: Beam length
numbers.value: 25 blocks, sweeping toward the target at 0.45 blocks/tick (faster when far off)

numbers.label: Max duration
numbers.value: 17 s (340 ticks)

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 35 s if any orb has fired within the first 5 s; otherwise only 5 s

numbers.label: Attack speed
numbers.value: −3.3 (main hand)

details.text: Each sickle gets a random colour theme when it's created: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, or prismatic (six different colours). The theme sets the orb, beam and glow colours and the colour of the Glass Cannon enchant. It's purely cosmetic.
Auto-targeting ignores players, villagers, tamed pets, armor stands and anything you aren't allowed to hurt. A lock-on can still pick any living thing you look at.
Auto-targeting and beams ignore walls: orbs can pick targets you have no line of sight to, and beams pass through blocks.
If a beam crosses something you aren't allowed to hurt, that orb disappears.
An orb with no target left vanishes. When every orb is gone, the volley ends early.
Taking any damage cancels your orbs, but only while the sickle is in your hand (or another equipped slot) at the moment you're hurt.
The sickle's ability is switched off at spawn and in the piñata world; you get an action-bar notice instead.

quirks.text: The code gives orbs a 30-damage hit when they touch a mob, but the orbs have no owner, so that hit never happens. Only the beams deal damage.

paintball-collectibles.summary: Souvenir paintballs from the Lumalympics paintball game. Throw one and the block it hits turns into blue or red wool, but only on your own screen.

use.text: Throw it like a snowball. The block it hits shows as blue or red wool to you only.

numbers.label: Block reach while held
numbers.value: −4.5 blocks (either hand)

details.text: The paint is only a visual on your own screen. Nobody else sees it and the real block never changes.
Paintballs pass through players and mobs with no effect.
Paintballs are switched off at spawn, in one of the event worlds and in the piñata world: you can't even equip them there.

quirks.text: Holding a paintball in your off-hand turns anything you launch (arrows from a bow, snowballs, eggs, ender pearls, tridents) into a paintball. The code swaps out every projectile you fire, not just the paintball itself.

config.text: Holding one lowers your block reach by 4.5 blocks. The normal survival reach is set by the game, not this plugin; on a default server it's 4.5, which would leave you unable to break or place blocks while a paintball is in either hand.

absorbent-sponges.summary: Reusable sponges. Place one into water (or lava, for the lava sponge) and every block of that fluid within 3 blocks disappears. The sponge never gets placed or used up.

use.text: Place the sponge into a water block (water sponge) or lava block (lava sponge). The placement is cancelled, the sponge stays in your hand, and the fluid around that spot is removed.

numbers.label: Radius
numbers.value: 3 blocks (sphere)

numbers.label: Uses
numbers.value: Unlimited; no cooldown

details.text: Both source and flowing fluid are removed.
Placing it anywhere that isn't the matching fluid (on dry ground, or a water sponge into lava) does nothing, and the sponge can't be placed as a block.
Removals are logged to the server's block-logging plugins under your name.

quirks.text: Waterlogged blocks (slabs, stairs, leaves and so on) keep their water. The code meant to drain them checks the wrong thing and never runs.

peach-plum-apron.summary: An elytra with two passives: while you wear it, beacon effects you receive are raised to a higher level, and anything you damage is given an Instant Health effect.

use.text: Wear it in the chest slot and stand in a beacon's range: each beacon effect you get is swapped for a stronger level.
Hit any living thing (up close or with your own arrows and other projectiles) while wearing or holding the apron, and it receives an Instant Health effect based on the damage you dealt.

numbers.label: Beacon boost
numbers.value: Effect level doubled: I becomes II, II becomes IV

numbers.label: Heal on hit
numbers.value: Instant Health I for hits under 16 damage, II for 16-31, III for 32-47 (one level per 16 damage)

numbers.label: Durability cost
numbers.value: A 50% roll for 1 point of wear each time a beacon refreshes an effect, plus a second 50% roll when the effect first lands or changes level

details.text: The beacon boost only works with the apron in your chest slot, and only for effects that come from a beacon (not potions or other sources).
Both abilities switch off once the item in your chest slot is down to its last point of durability.
The Instant Health goes to whatever you hit, including hostile mobs and other players. It does not heal you.

quirks.text: The tooltip says 25% of the damage is healed, but the code turns that 25% into a whole Instant Health level instead (level I for any hit under 16 damage, II from 16, and so on), so the result is not a straight 25% of the damage.
The tooltip says beacon effects are boosted by 50%, but the code doubles the effect level.
When a beacon effect first lands, the apron rolls for wear twice, so it can take 2 points at once. A comment in the code asks whether this is intentional.
The heal-on-hit doesn't need the apron to be worn: it also works while the apron is held in either hand. It only checks that whatever is in your chest slot isn't about to break.

config.text: How much health each Instant Health level restores, and the fact that Instant Health hurts undead mobs (zombies, skeletons and so on) instead of healing them, are the game's own rules, not this item's code. Not tested here.
The wear is applied through the game's normal item-damage handling, so how much the apron's Unbreaking enchant cancels depends on the game, not this item. Not tested here.

architects-compass.summary: An off-hand add-on for the Builder's Wand. With the wand in your main hand and the compass in your off-hand, the wand builds a flat ring of blocks instead of a path.

use.text: Hold a Builder's Wand in your main hand and the compass in your off-hand, then right-click a block. The block you clicked is the one that gets copied, and the ring is centred on the space next to the face you clicked.
Look outward to set the size. The radius follows the flat distance from the centre to the block you're looking at, and a preview of the ring follows your aim.
Left-click to build the ring, or press swap (F) to cancel.

numbers.label: Max radius
numbers.value: 22 blocks (you must be looking at a block within 22 blocks)

numbers.label: Preview refresh
numbers.value: Every 0.15 s (3 ticks)

numbers.label: Cost
numbers.value: 1 of the copied block per ring spot

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 11 s on the tooltip, but 4 s in practice (see quirks); only starts after a successful build

details.text: The ring is flat, at the same height as its centre. It only fills spots that were empty or replaceable (air, grass, water and so on) when the preview was drawn.
It copies the exact block you clicked, including which way it faces. Leaves placed this way never decay.
You need enough of that block in your inventory for the whole ring. If you're short, nothing is placed and red dust shows instead. It's free in creative mode.
Claims are respected: you can't start on a block you aren't allowed to build on, and building stops at the first ring spot you can't build in.
It can't copy ores, chests, crops and other growing blocks, doors, pistons, or blocks that have no item form.
The preview is cancelled if you teleport, log out, open a container, or take the wand or compass out of your hands.

quirks.text: The tooltip says right-click centres the circle on you, but it's actually centred on the space next to the block face you clicked.

The tooltip says the cooldown is 11 s, but the Builder's Wand in your main hand reacts to the left-click first. It builds the ring and puts only its own 4-second cooldown on the compass, so the compass is ready again after 4 s.
Blocks for the whole ring are taken before anything is placed. If building stops early at a claim border, you don't get back the blocks for the spots that were skipped.

config.text: Placed blocks are logged under your name if the server runs CoreProtect. With Prism, only blocks that were replaced (not empty air) are logged; the new blocks themselves aren't.

grow-berries.summary: Reusable berries. Eating them makes you twice as big for one minute and doubles your health, speed, reach and several other stats, then you shrink back.

use.text: Eat them like normal food, from either hand. The berries are not used up.

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 2 min (120 s), starting when you eat

numbers.label: Stat boost
numbers.value: +100% of the base value on 9 stats

details.text: Doubled stats: size, max health, movement speed, jump strength, safe fall distance, block reach, entity reach, underwater breath and step height.
When you grow, your health is scaled up so you keep the same share of your new, doubled maximum.
You can eat them on a full hunger bar. They give no food or saturation.
Eating them while on cooldown just shows the time left.

They only work in the main worlds (overworld, nether, end, seasons, terralith) and the resource worlds (overworld, nether, end, desert). Everywhere else they are fully disabled: you can't eat them or even move them into your hotbar.
Teleporting into a world where they're disabled shrinks you back right away, even if you're no longer carrying the berries.
They can't be planted as cave vines or put in a composter.

smugglers-cask.summary: A barrel you wear as a hat. Sneak while wearing it and you become a small, invisible barrel that can't move, and mobs lose track of you.

use.text: Wear it in the helmet slot (it equips like armour), then sneak while standing on something solid.
If you sneak in mid-air, the barrel closes as soon as you land on a solid block, as long as you're still sneaking.
Stop sneaking to pop back out.

numbers.label: Mob forget radius
numbers.value: 32 blocks

numbers.label: Barrel seen by players within
numbers.value: 64 blocks

numbers.label: Refresh
numbers.value: Every 1 s (20 ticks)

numbers.label: Size while hidden
numbers.value: 0.35x normal

numbers.label: Invisibility
numbers.value: 5 s, renewed every second while hidden

details.text: While hidden you're snapped to the middle of the block and can't walk or jump, but you can still look around. Your camera is pulled far out behind you, you shrink and turn invisible, and players nearby see a barrel standing where you are.
Nothing can start targeting you. Every second, mobs within 32 blocks that were targeting you forget you: creepers stop swelling, Wardens drop their anger at you, and shulker bullets stop homing in.
The disguise ends when you stop sneaking, take the cask off, teleport off the spot, die or log out.
Nothing in its code stops players from attacking you. The protection only covers mob targeting.
It can't be placed as a barrel block.

quirks.text: Coming out of the barrel removes all Invisibility from you, including any from a potion you drank earlier.

prospectors-spyglass.summary: Look through it, and ores up to 18 blocks away in a narrow line where you're aiming glow through the ground. Only you can see the glow.

use.text: Scope in (hold right-click) with it in either hand. Ores near your crosshair are outlined in their ore colour.

numbers.label: Range
numbers.value: 18 blocks

numbers.label: Search cone
numbers.value: About 1.7 blocks wide at your eye, spreading 3.5 degrees each side of your crosshair (about 4 blocks wide at 18 blocks)

numbers.label: Scan rate
numbers.value: Every 0.2 s (4 ticks) while scoped

details.text: Shows the game's coal, iron, copper, gold, redstone, emerald, lapis and diamond ore groups plus nether quartz ore. Ancient debris is not shown.
Outlines disappear when you stop scoping, look away, move more than 20 blocks from them, switch to a hotbar slot without the spyglass, swap hands, or log out.
It only scans loaded chunks and never shows anything behind you.

config.text: The outline is only sent to your screen through the ProtocolLib plugin. Without it, the outlines don't show up.

fiberglass-rod.summary: A fishing rod that fishes in lava instead of water. Fish caught in lava come out cooked, and there's a small chance of a bonus item with a fire theme.

use.text: Cast into lava with it in either hand. The bobber floats on the lava, and bites work like normal fishing.

numbers.label: Bonus catch
numbers.value: 10% of lava catches are replaced by one of 11 bonus items (equal odds)

numbers.label: Catch fire protection
numbers.value: 5 s (100 ticks)

numbers.label: Hooked mob burn
numbers.value: 5 s (100 ticks)

numbers.label: Bite window
numbers.value: 1-2 s to reel in after a bite

numbers.label: Max line length
numbers.value: 32 blocks (you must keep a fishing rod in hand)

details.text: Swaps for lava catches that aren't bonus items: raw cod becomes cooked cod, raw salmon becomes cooked salmon, lily pad becomes crimson fungus, ink sac becomes glow ink sac, and a water bottle becomes a glass bottle. Other catches are unchanged.

Bonus items: beetroot soup, 2 golden dandelions, enchanted golden apple, 2 golden carrots, golden apple, ominous bottle, 4 glowstone dust, blaze rod, fire charge, 3 dragon's breath, potion of Fire Resistance.
Caught items can't be hurt for 5 seconds, so they survive the trip out of the lava.
It can't fish in water. A bobber that lands in water fizzles out and disappears.
The rod's Lure and Luck of the Sea enchants still apply.
In the Nether, fishing gets the speed boost that rain normally gives. Fishing under a roof isn't slowed down.
If you hold a fishing rod in both hands, none of this happens.

quirks.text: Cooking, the bonus roll and the fire protection only happen if the bobber's own block is lava when you reel in. The rod's own code notes that a floating bobber can sit in the air block just above the lava; a catch reeled in at that moment comes out unchanged and unprotected.

config.text: The Nether speed-up only applies while the bobber counts as 'rain-influenced', a server-side fishing setting this item never changes (on by default on Paper servers). Not tested here.

undertow-spade.summary: A shovel that puts the drops of every block you break straight into your inventory.

use.text: Break blocks with it in your main hand.

details.text: You get the block's normal drops for this spade. Anything that doesn't fit in your inventory falls at the block.
Experience orbs aren't touched and still drop on the ground.
It only acts on breaks that were allowed. If a claim or another plugin cancels the break, nothing happens.

config.text: The spade switches off the block's own drops and gives you the standard drops directly. Whether extra drops from other plugins (for example mcMMO bonus drops) still appear depends on how those plugins work. Not tested here.

ignition-cutlass.summary: A sword that sets nearby mobs on fire while you hold it, and gives you Speed, Haste and Regeneration whenever you deal damage.

use.text: Hold it in either hand. Every 3.5 seconds, every eligible mob within 10 blocks takes 1 heart of damage and catches fire.
Damage anything while holding it to get Speed I, Regeneration I and Haste I.

numbers.label: Aura interval
numbers.value: Every 3.5 s (70 ticks)

numbers.label: Aura radius
numbers.value: 10 blocks

numbers.label: Aura damage
numbers.value: 2 (1 heart) per pulse

numbers.label: Aura burn
numbers.value: 20 s (400 ticks)

numbers.label: On-hit buffs
numbers.value: Speed I, Regeneration I, Haste I for 8 s (160 ticks)

details.text: The aura skips players, named mobs, tamed pets, leashed animals, and anything you're not allowed to hurt (for example in a claim). Everything else is hit, including passive animals and villagers.
The aura's damage isn't credited to you.
The buffs trigger on any damage you deal with the cutlass in either hand, including arrows.

quirks.text: The tooltip only mentions speed and haste, but you also get Regeneration I.

umbra-scimitar.summary: Right-click to open a 10-second gravity well at the block you're looking at. It drags mobs in and damages them every second, then explodes, flinging them outward and setting them on fire.

use.text: Right-click with it in your main hand while looking at a block up to 75 blocks away.

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 30 s (600 ticks); not used if you aren't looking at a block

numbers.label: Target range
numbers.value: 75 blocks

numbers.label: Duration
numbers.value: 10 s (200 ticks)

numbers.label: Pull radius
numbers.value: 15 blocks

numbers.label: Well damage
numbers.value: 8 every second (10 times) to mobs within 16 blocks

numbers.label: Tether
numbers.value: Mobs just outside 15 blocks are tethered and pulled in, taking 5 damage every 0.5 s until they're within 5 blocks

numbers.label: Final burst
numbers.value: 25 damage and 10 s of fire (200 ticks) to mobs within 16 blocks

details.text: Only mobs are hurt. Players, armour stands, named mobs, tamed pets, leashed animals, and anything you're not allowed to hurt (for example in a claim) are left alone.
All of its damage is credited to you.
Each once-a-second damage pulse briefly stops everything in the well, so the pull is jerky.
Disabled in the Pinata world (incu:pinata).

quirks.text: The pull also catches things that aren't alive, such as dropped items, XP orbs, arrows, minecarts and boats, and drags them into the well.

incursion-blunderhorn.summary: A goat horn that works like a shotgun. Right-click to blast a short cone that hurts every living thing in front of you, hardest up close.

use.text: Right-click with it in your main hand.

numbers.label: Range
numbers.value: 6.5 blocks

numbers.label: Cone width
numbers.value: 45 degrees

numbers.label: Damage
numbers.value: 90 at point-blank, dropping evenly to 13.5 at 6.5 blocks

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 1.5 s (30 ticks)

numbers.label: Bosses
numbers.value: Elder Guardian, Ender Dragon, Wither and Warden take half damage

details.text: It hits everything in the cone at once but can't hit through walls. Blocks you can walk through (grass, flowers and so on) and barrier blocks don't stop it.
It skips you, tamed pets and named mobs. Players can be hit wherever PvP and claims allow it.
The damage is dealt as a normal hit from you (not true damage), so claim and protection plugins can still block it.
All your Blunderhorns share one cooldown: a second Blunderhorn can't fire until it runs out.
It's unbreakable and plays no horn tune.

config.text: The cooldown is put on goat horns as an item type. Whether that also blocks ordinary goat horns you carry depends on the game's own cooldown rules. Not tested here.

incursion-overwatch.summary: A spyglass that works as a sniper rifle. Hold right-click to charge, then release to fire a beam up to 100 blocks that goes through every mob in its path and does double damage on headshots.

use.text: Hold right-click with it in your main hand. A charge bar fills on screen and shows READY once charged.
Release to fire. If you let go before it's charged, or after switching hotbar slots, nothing fires and there's no cooldown.

numbers.label: Charge time
numbers.value: 0.8 s (16 ticks)

numbers.label: Range
numbers.value: 100 blocks

numbers.label: Damage
numbers.value: 40 per mob hit, 80 on a headshot

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 2.25 s (45 ticks) after firing

numbers.label: Charge limit
numbers.value: Gives up without firing after 60 s of holding

numbers.label: Bosses
numbers.value: Elder Guardian, Ender Dragon, Wither and Warden take half damage

details.text: The beam goes through mobs, hitting every one whose body it crosses, until it reaches a solid block. Blocks you can walk through and barrier blocks don't stop it.
A headshot shows a HEADSHOT title with the distance. Headshots on the Ender Dragon hit its head directly.

It skips you, tamed pets and named mobs. Players can be hit wherever PvP and claims allow it. The damage is dealt as a normal hit from you (not true damage), so claim and protection plugins can still block it.
All your Overwatches share one cooldown: a second one can't start charging until it runs out.
It's unbreakable.

config.text: The cooldown is put on spyglasses as an item type. Whether that also stops you using other spyglasses (such as the Prospector's Spyglass) for 2.25 s depends on the game's own cooldown rules. Not tested here.

stormveil-reaper.summary: Right-click to hang storm clouds over mobs near where you're looking. For 45 seconds, those mobs take extra damage from players' hits and don't get knocked back. When one dies, its loot rains down from the cloud, sometimes with extra and sometimes swallowed completely.

use.text: Right-click with it in your main hand. It aims at the mob you're looking at (up to 50 blocks), otherwise the block you're looking at (up to 15 blocks), otherwise a point 10 blocks ahead. Every eligible mob within 6 blocks of that spot gets a cloud.

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 23 s; only used if at least one mob got a cloud

numbers.label: Cloud radius
numbers.value: 6 blocks around the aimed spot

numbers.label: Cloud duration
numbers.value: 45 s (900 ticks)

numbers.label: Damage bonus
numbers.value: Each hit is multiplied by a random amount between 1x and 2x

numbers.label: Bounty chance
numbers.value: 12%: drops rain down, with the mob's normal loot increased by a random 1.5x-2x

numbers.label: Void chance
numbers.value: 10%: all drops are destroyed

numbers.label: Otherwise
numbers.value: 78%: the normal drops rain down from the cloud unchanged

numbers.label: Rained drops won't stack for
numbers.value: 30 s (600 ticks)

details.text: The damage bonus applies to direct hits from any player, with any weapon, not only the Reaper. Arrows and other projectiles don't get it.
Clouded mobs take no knockback from players' hits.
The loot effect happens no matter who or what kills a clouded mob.
Rained drops fall one at a time from the cloud, over a small area around where the mob died. XP isn't affected.
Only mobs get clouds. Players, armour stands, mobs you can't hurt (for example in a claim), and mobs that already have a cloud are skipped.
In the Pinata world (incu:pinata), right-clicking, the damage bonus and the no-knockback effect are switched off for players standing there, but the loot effect still happens.

quirks.text: The tooltip says a cloud may rain double the loot, but the bonus is a random 1.5x to 2x, and it only multiplies items from the mob's normal loot table (not, for example, gear it picked up).

incursion-eggs.summary: Reusable throwing eggs that explode where they land and damage everything within 4.5 blocks. The Cryo Egg also freezes and slows what it hits; the Unstable Egg is just the explosion. Press swap (F) to switch between the egg types.

use.text: Right-click to throw, from either hand. The egg isn't used up.
Press swap (F) while holding one to turn it into the next egg type: Unstable to Cryo, Cryo to Incendiary, Incendiary back to Unstable.

numbers.label: Blast radius
numbers.value: 4.5 blocks

numbers.label: Damage
numbers.value: 65 at the centre, dropping evenly to about 9.75 at the edge

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 3.5 s (70 ticks)

numbers.label: Cryo Egg: Slowness
numbers.value: Slowness III for 5 s (100 ticks)

numbers.label: Cryo Egg: freeze
numbers.value: Target's freeze meter (the one powder snow fills) set to at least 200

numbers.label: Bosses
numbers.value: Elder Guardian, Ender Dragon, Wither and Warden take half damage

details.text: It explodes when it hits a block or a mob. Every living thing in range is hurt except you, tamed pets and named mobs, with distance measured to each target's centre. Players can be hit wherever PvP and claims allow it.
The explosion goes through walls, because its line-of-sight check is switched off in the code. It doesn't break blocks.
Your movement adds to the throw speed.
A custom name or lore you give an egg is remembered for each egg type and comes back when you switch to that type again.
They can't be fired from dispensers or used in crafting.

config.text: The cooldown is put on the egg's underlying item type. Whether that also blocks throwing ordinary eggs of the same colour depends on the game's own cooldown rules. Not tested here.

aestiva-barillas.summary: Netherite boots that make you bounce off surfaces and push back the height at which falls start to hurt. They do this through two attributes on the boots, with no plugin code running.

numbers.label: Bounciness
numbers.value: +1.0 (only while worn on the feet)

numbers.label: Safe fall distance
numbers.value: +10 blocks (only while worn on the feet)

details.text: The item has no ability code of its own. The bounce and the softer landings come from the two attributes, and the Feather Falling VII on the boots cuts fall damage further.
Both attributes only count in the feet slot. Holding the boots in your hand does nothing.

config.text: How much you bounce is decided by the game server's handling of the Bounciness attribute, not by this plugin, so the feel depends on the server software and version.

sunbrella-nouveau.summary: A helmet with three abilities while worn. Full-power sword swings throw a fan of three wind crescents, the helmet lowers your air drag, and holding sneak while falling opens a steerable paraglider canopy that cancels fall damage.

use.text: Crescent Gale: wear it on your head, hold a sword in your main hand, and left-click (swing) with the attack meter at least 90% charged. The same check also runs when you land a melee hit.
Drift: while falling, hold sneak to open the canopy and keep holding sneak to stay under it. Look down to dive and build speed, and look up to flare, which trades speed for lift.

numbers.label: Crescent volley
numbers.value: 3 crescents at -14°, 0° and +14°, launched 0.1 s apart

numbers.label: Crescent cooldown
numbers.value: 0.5 s (10 ticks)

numbers.label: Crescent damage
numbers.value: 34% of (your attack damage + the sword's Sharpness bonus), at least 3 per crescent. Example: netherite sword with Sharpness V is about 3.7

numbers.label: Crescent range
numbers.value: 17 blocks, travelling 1.1 blocks per tick (22 blocks/s)

numbers.label: Crescent hit size
numbers.value: 1.7 blocks around the crescent sideways, about 1.45 blocks up and down

numbers.label: Sword wear
numbers.value: 1 durability per volley

numbers.label: Air drag
numbers.value: -0.5 air drag modifier while worn on the head

numbers.label: Canopy speed
numbers.value: cruises at 0.55 blocks/tick (11 blocks/s), dives up to 2.1 blocks/tick (42 blocks/s)

numbers.label: Canopy climb
numbers.value: at most 0.38 blocks/tick upward while flaring

details.text: Each crescent hits each creature at most once, and it clears the target's short post-hit immunity right before hitting, so all three crescents can land on the same target.
Crescents stop at the first solid block and pass through open or non-solid space. They hit players too, but only where protection plugins (WorldGuard/Towny) allow you to damage them.
Damage done by a crescent can't trigger another volley. Arrows and other projectiles you shoot don't trigger one either.
The canopy only opens when you're falling faster than 0.08 blocks per tick and at least about 0.6 blocks above the ground. It won't open while flying, gliding with an elytra, riding, or in water.

The canopy closes when you let go of sneak, touch the ground, enter water, start flying, gliding or riding, or take the helmet off. While it's open your fall distance resets every tick, so landing does no damage.
Slipstream is only visual: colored wind streaks and a whirl sound appear once you move faster than 15.5 blocks per second.
Crescent Gale is switched off in the Piñata world. The canopy, the wind streaks and the lower air drag still work there, because the world block isn't applied to movement.

builders-wand.summary: A building tool that copies a block along a path you point at. Right-click a block to start a preview line of up to 48 blocks, aim to shape it, and left-click to place it using blocks from your inventory. Left-clicking a block without a preview rotates it.

use.text: Right-click a block with the wand to start build mode. The preview starts from the side you clicked and runs to the spot in front of whatever face you're aiming at.
Left-click anywhere to confirm. This places copies of the block you first right-clicked, keeping its exact state (orientation, half, and so on).
Press the swap key (F) to cancel the preview.
With no preview open, left-click a block to turn it to its next direction or axis. On fences, panes and similar blocks it toggles the side you clicked.

numbers.label: Max path length
numbers.value: 48 blocks

numbers.label: Aim reach
numbers.value: 48 blocks

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 4 s after a successful placement

numbers.label: Cost
numbers.value: 1 of the block's item per block in the path (free in Creative)

details.text: The path goes around solid blocks, moving one block at a time in any of the six directions, so it can climb and bend. Only non-solid spaces count as open.

You can't start from ores, chests, crops and other growing plants, doors, pistons, or blocks that have no item form. Trying shows red dust instead. Red dust also appears while the wand is on cooldown or where you can't build.
If you don't have enough of the block for the whole path, nothing is placed and red dust traces the path.
Placement respects claims (WorldGuard/Towny) and stops at the first spot you can't build in. Leaves placed by the wand never decay.

The preview uses small ghost blocks that other players can see too. It is cancelled when you teleport, log out, stop holding the wand in your main hand, or open a container (checked about once a second).

quirks.text: The items for the whole path are taken before the claim check. If the path runs into a spot you can't build in, placement stops there, but you still lose the items for the blocks that weren't placed.
Non-solid blocks in the path, such as grass, flowers, torches and water, are overwritten without dropping anything.

The wand also reacts when it's in your off-hand. Your left- and right-clicks on blocks are cancelled, and left-clicking a block rotates it, so keep the wand out of your off-hand while you mine or build normally.

lodestar-compass.summary: A biome-finding compass. Left-click to scan for the nearest different biomes between 300 and 1,000 blocks away, then right-click to step through them. The needle and action bar show each biome's name and distance.

use.text: Left-click to scan. A ring of particles sweeps over the ground around you, and when it finishes the compass points at the nearest biome it found.
Right-click (either hand) to switch to the next biome in the list. It loops back to the first after the last.

numbers.label: Scan range
numbers.value: 300 to 1,000 blocks from where you stand (horizontal distance)

numbers.label: Results
numbers.value: up to 12 biomes, nearest first

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 1 s, shared by scanning and switching

numbers.label: Reading expires
numbers.value: after you move more than 4,000 blocks from the scan spot, or change worlds

numbers.label: Sweep effect
numbers.value: 75-block radius

details.text: It lists each biome type once, at its nearest point, and skips the biome you're standing in.

It reads the world generator's biome map, so it works for land nobody has loaded yet. It samples every 16 blocks and then narrows each hit down on a 4-block grid, so the edge it points to can be a few blocks off.
In the Overworld it checks biomes at your height or sea level, whichever is higher. In other dimensions it uses your height.
Biomes added by datapacks show their source in grey brackets on the action bar, and as 'Charted by' on the compass tooltip.
The scan-sweep particles are shown only to you.
Right-clicking a lodestone does nothing, so the compass can't be re-bound. Right-clicking a door, chest or other usable block uses that block instead, unless you're sneaking.

quirks.text: The scan is only remembered while the server is running. It's cleared if you log out while holding the compass, and after a restart you have to scan again.
Every new reading swaps the compass in your hand for a freshly made copy, so a custom name or any enchantments you added to it are lost.

infinite-tropical-fish-bucket.summary: A tropical fish bucket that never empties. Every use places water, and it releases a new tropical fish at most once every 8 seconds.

use.text: Use it like a normal bucket (either hand) to pour water. The bucket is never used up.

numbers.label: Fish cooldown
numbers.value: 8 s between released fish (water has no cooldown)

details.text: Pouring respects claims (WorldGuard/Towny). It waterlogs waterloggable blocks, and replaceable blocks in the way (like grass) break and drop as usual.
Released fish are marked as coming from a bucket. Fish from this bucket give no Jobs experience or pay.

quirks.text: In the Nether the water evaporates, but a fish is still released (if off cooldown) with no water around it.

config.text: The no-Jobs-reward rule only applies when the Jobs plugin is installed.

infinite-air-bucket.summary: An empty bucket that never fills. It deletes water, lava and powder snow instead of picking them up, and can also remove flowing (non-source) water and lava. Press F while holding it to refill your breath.

use.text: Use it on a source block of water or lava, on powder snow, or on a waterlogged block to remove the fluid. The bucket stays empty.
Right-click flowing water or lava within your normal reach to remove that block too, which a vanilla bucket can't do.
Press the swap key (F) with it in either hand to refill your air bar to full.

numbers.label: Air refill cooldown
numbers.value: 3 s (60 ticks)

details.text: Draining respects claims (WorldGuard/Towny).
The air refill does nothing if your air is already full, and the cooldown gives no message.

quirks.text: Pressing F while holding it never swaps your hands, even when your air is full or the refill is on cooldown.

tidewarden-barding.summary: Unbreakable diamond armor for a nautilus. While your nautilus wears it, it's made invulnerable, never despawns, and leaves a glowing blue trail.

use.text: Put it on a nautilus as body armor. A conduit chime and a particle burst confirm it's active.

numbers.label: Trail
numbers.value: particles every 0.15 s (3 ticks), only while a player is nearby to see them

details.text: While worn, the nautilus is made invulnerable and is kept from despawning.
Remove the barding and the invulnerability goes away. An untamed nautilus can despawn again.
The protection comes back on its own when the nautilus's chunk reloads, for example after a restart.
The barding itself is unbreakable.

quirks.text: 'It will not wander off' only means it won't despawn. Nothing stops the nautilus from swimming away.

lumarine-charm.summary: A Lumarine minigame participation token. This plugin gives it no ability, so its value is as a collectible.

details.text: The item class has no ability code, and nothing else in LumaItems checks for the charm.

config.text: The tooltip hints at a future use ('keep it around'). If that exists, it lives outside this plugin, for example in an event or another server plugin.

gala-hatchet.summary: A netherite axe that sometimes fires a volley of fireworks when you break logs or leaves. The rockets steer toward nearby wood and blast away the logs and leaves around where they explode.

use.text: Break logs or leaves with it in your main hand. Each break has a small chance to launch the volley.

numbers.label: Trigger chance
numbers.value: 5% per log or leaf block broken

numbers.label: Rockets per volley
numbers.value: 1 to 9 (random), launched 0.1 s apart

numbers.label: Fuse
numbers.value: at most 0.7 s (14 ticks) before it goes off

numbers.label: Blast radius
numbers.value: up to 2 blocks, with ragged edges (1.2-2 blocks)

numbers.label: Wood-seeking range
numbers.value: 8 blocks

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 0.25 s between volleys

details.text: Rockets fan out in a ring. Any rocket whose path wouldn't reach a tree turns toward a nearby log it has a clear line to, choosing from the 4 logs closest to its direction.
Each blast breaks only logs and leaves, and only where you're allowed to build (WorldGuard/Towny). Blocks drop as if broken by hand, and blast-broken blocks don't set off more volleys.
Players holding a Gala Hatchet in either hand take no damage from these rockets.

quirks.text: Any log block counts, including player-built log walls, as long as you have build rights there.

config.text: The rockets are real fireworks. Nothing in this plugin shields other players or mobs who aren't holding a Gala Hatchet, so they may take firework damage (depends on the game and protection plugins, not tested).

axiom-mattock-core.summary: A voucher. Right-click it to use it up and get one Axiom Mattock, either Flux or Union at even odds.

numbers.label: Odds
numbers.value: 50% Union, 50% Flux

details.text: The mattock is added straight to your inventory.

config.text: If your inventory is full, the server's own give logic decides what happens to the mattock. Normally it drops at your feet (depends on the game, not tested).

axiom-mattock.summary: A netherite pickaxe with +2 block reach. Right-click to spend 10 seconds carving out an 8-block sphere around the block you're looking at, using beams that break stone- and dirt-type blocks. Union fires straight up-and-down beams; Flux fires them in random directions.

use.text: Right-click while looking at a block up to 25 blocks away. The effect is centered on top of that block. If you're not looking at a block, nothing happens and no cooldown starts.

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 3 min (180 s)

numbers.label: Duration
numbers.value: 10 s (200 ticks)

numbers.label: Radius
numbers.value: 8 blocks (sphere)

numbers.label: Beams
numbers.value: 2 per tick (about 400 over the whole effect)

numbers.label: Targeting range
numbers.value: 25 blocks

numbers.label: Durability cost
numbers.value: 50 per use

numbers.label: Reach bonus
numbers.value: +2 block interaction range while held in either hand

details.text: Beams break blocks that are mined with a pickaxe or shovel and are softer than obsidian. Obsidian, crying obsidian, bedrock and anything else as hard or harder are left alone.
Each beam stops at the first block you aren't allowed to build on (WorldGuard/Towny).
With the mattock in your main hand, its Silk Touch applies to what the beams break, so you get the blocks themselves. Broken ores drop no experience.
Union beams all run vertically. Flux beams each pick a random direction.

quirks.text: It doesn't spare builds. Anything pickaxe- or shovel-mineable and softer than obsidian inside the sphere gets broken, as long as you have build rights there.
There's no hand check, so right-clicking with the mattock in your off-hand also fires it.

pink-ayune-tools.summary: A gamble on every ore (mattock) or log (hatchet) you break. Some breaks 'burst': the block stays in place and its drops pop out anyway. Some other breaks drop nothing. A burst makes the next burst more likely.

use.text: Mine ores with the mattock or logs with the hatchet, with the tool in your main hand.

numbers.label: Burst chance
numbers.value: 25% per block, or 35% right after a burst

numbers.label: Empty chance
numbers.value: 18% of non-burst breaks (13.5% of all breaks normally, 11.7% during a streak)

numbers.label: Pickup delay on burst drops
numbers.value: 1 s

details.text: On a burst, the break is cancelled, so the block stays in place. You get the drops the tool would normally give (including Fortune V), scattered one item at a time.
On an 'empty' break, the block breaks but drops no items.
The 35% streak lasts until a break doesn't burst. It doesn't climb past 35%, and the mattock and hatchet keep separate streaks.
The mattock counts every ore, including deepslate and nether gold ore and nether quartz ore. Ancient debris doesn't count.
The hatchet turns burst drops into the matching bark-covered wood block (oak log gives oak wood, crimson stem gives crimson hyphae, and so on).
Burst drops are kept from merging into stacks for 1.5 s.
Protected blocks aren't affected. If a claim stops you breaking the block, neither roll happens.

quirks.text: A burst on a mangrove log gives mangrove propagules instead of mangrove wood. The log-to-wood table maps mangrove to the wrong item.
The hatchet also rolls on stripped logs and on wood blocks, which have no entry in that table. A burst on those gives nothing, and the block just stays.

config.text: Because a burst cancels the break, the tool should take no durability and ores should give no experience on a burst (depends on the game, not tested).

mistrium-rod.summary: A fishing rod that shortens the bite timing when you cast and keeps a little rain cloud over your head. The rain turns dirt into grass and lava into obsidian where it lands.

use.text: Hold it in either hand to get the rain cloud. Cast it as usual to get the shorter bite timing.

numbers.label: Lure time
numbers.value: cut to 22% of normal (both the shortest and the longest)

numbers.label: Extra durability per cast
numbers.value: 7 (before Unbreaking)

numbers.label: Rain
numbers.value: 2 drops per tick from about 3 blocks above your eyes, within 1.5 blocks sideways, falling up to 24 blocks

details.text: The fishing bonus is skipped if you hold a fishing rod in both hands.
Raindrops that land on dirt turn it into a grass block, and drops that land on a lava source turn it into obsidian. This only happens where you're allowed to build (WorldGuard/Towny).
The cloud stops while you're jumping, underwater, or in the Nether.

config.text: Which part of fishing the shortened lure time covers is decided by the game, not this plugin. It should be the time between a fish appearing and it biting, not the wait before a fish appears, which Lure V on the rod shortens the usual way (depends on the game, not tested).
The rod also switches off rain's influence on each cast's timing, so real weather shouldn't speed it up (depends on the game, not tested).

magmatic-shovel.summary: A netherite shovel that adds a glass block when you dig sand or red sand.

use.text: Dig sand or red sand with the shovel in your main hand.

details.text: Red sand gives plain glass, not a colored glass.

quirks.text: The sand isn't replaced. Its normal drop is left alone and the glass drops as an extra item, so each sand block gives you both sand and glass.

incursion-spitter.summary: A pufferfish gun that can't be eaten. Right-click to spit a fast, arcing jet of water that hits the first creature in its path, dealing less damage the farther it travels.

use.text: Right-click with it in your main hand (the off-hand doesn't work).

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 0.25 s (5 ticks)

numbers.label: Damage
numbers.value: 15 up close, falling to 11.25 at max range

numbers.label: Range
numbers.value: 22 blocks of travel

numbers.label: Speed
numbers.value: 1.2 blocks per tick, aimed 10° above where you look, then arcing down

details.text: The spit stops at the first solid block or the first creature it touches. Barriers don't stop it.

Tamed pets and mobs with a custom name take no damage (the spit still stops on them). Boss mobs (Ender Dragon, Wither, Warden, Elder Guardian) take half damage. You can't hit yourself, and other players can only be hit where protection plugins allow.
The cooldown uses the game's own item cooldown for pufferfish.

config.text: The damage is dealt as a hit from you, so the target's armor and Protection should reduce it (depends on the game, not tested).

Nothing in the plugin clears a target's short immunity after being hit, and spits can fire every 0.25 s, so back-to-back spits on one target may not all do full damage (depends on the game, not tested).

darksun-scythe.summary: A netherite hoe that reaps an area when you right-click. A small zone at your target is hit by 7 waves of slashes over about 2 seconds, and the first wave stops and heavily slows what it hits.

use.text: Right-click with the scythe in your main hand. It targets the creature you're looking at (up to 50 blocks away), otherwise the top of the block you're looking at (up to 10 blocks away), otherwise a spot 10 blocks in front of you.

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 8 s

numbers.label: Damage
numbers.value: 14 per wave, 7 waves (one right away, then every 0.35 s)

numbers.label: Area
numbers.value: 2 blocks out from the target point and 2.5 blocks up and down (box-shaped)

numbers.label: Root (first wave only)
numbers.value: stops the target's movement and gives Slowness IV for 2.8 s

details.text: The zone stays where you aimed. Moving away or looking elsewhere doesn't move it.
It skips you and armor stands. Other players, pets and animals can be hit wherever protection plugins (WorldGuard/Towny) allow.
Disabled in the Piñata world.

quirks.text: Right-clicking while on cooldown does nothing and shows no message.

config.text: Nothing in the plugin clears a target's short immunity after being hit, and the waves come 0.35 s apart, so a target standing in the zone may not take damage from every wave (depends on the game, not tested).

incursion-incendiary-egg.summary: A reusable throwing egg. Right-click to throw it, and it explodes where it lands, damaging creatures within 4.5 blocks and setting them on fire. Press F to cycle it to the next egg variant.

use.text: Right-click to throw. The egg in your hand isn't used up.
Press the swap key (F) with it in either hand to turn it into the next variant: Incendiary, then Unstable, then Cryo, then back to Incendiary.

numbers.label: Cooldown
numbers.value: 3.5 s (70 ticks)

numbers.label: Damage
numbers.value: 65 at the center, falling off with distance to 9.75 at the edge

numbers.label: Blast radius
numbers.value: 4.5 blocks, measured to the center of each creature's body

numbers.label: Burn
numbers.value: at least 5 s of fire (100 ticks) on everything hit

numbers.label: Throw speed
numbers.value: 1.5 blocks per tick, plus your own movement

details.text: Tamed pets and name-tagged mobs are neither hurt nor set on fire. Boss mobs take half damage. You can't hit yourself, and other players are only hit where protection plugins allow.
A custom name or lore you give the egg is kept for that variant when you cycle through the others and back.
It stacks to 1, can't be used in crafting, and dispensers won't fire it.

quirks.text: The explosion goes through walls. A line-of-sight check exists in the code but is switched off.

witching-boots.summary: While worn, these boots keep Jump Boost II on you and make you walk faster. The effect comes off the moment the boots leave your feet.

use.text: Wear them in the boots slot. Jump Boost II is topped up every 3.5 seconds while they're on your feet.

numbers.label: Jump Boost
numbers.value: Level II, 17 s per refresh (340 ticks), refreshed every 3.5 s

numbers.label: Movement speed
numbers.value: +0.025 (feet slot only)

quirks.text: Taking the boots off removes every Jump Boost effect you have, including one from a potion or beacon.

witching-stocks.summary: Gives you one mid-air double jump: press sneak while you're off the ground and you're flung up and forward. You get the jump back when you land. The leggings also double your safe fall distance.

use.text: Press sneak while airborne (at least about 1 block above solid ground) to launch in the direction you're looking.
The double jump recharges once you're standing on a solid block again.

numbers.label: Launch
numbers.value: 0.6 × your look direction forward, 0.7 upward (replaces your current momentum)

numbers.label: Uses per jump
numbers.value: 1 until you land

numbers.label: Safe fall distance
numbers.value: +100% of base (leg slot)

details.text: Doesn't work in water or while using creative-style flight.

quirks.text: The tooltip says "while falling", but the code only checks that you're off the ground. It works on the way up too.
The double jump doesn't check the leggings slot. Holding the Stocks in your main hand or off-hand also gives you the double jump, though the safe-fall bonus only applies when they're worn.

devourers-apron.summary: When you kill a creature, a soul orb floats where it died for 5 seconds. Press your swap-hands key (F) in time to pull the orb into you for Regeneration plus Absorption and Health Boost that scale with the victim's max health.

use.text: Kill any creature while wearing the apron (holding it in either hand also counts). A soul orb appears at the victim's eye height.

Press F within 5 seconds while within 70 blocks of the orb, with the apron still on you (worn or in either hand). The orb streaks into you and the buffs land when it reaches you. The hand swap is cancelled.

numbers.label: Orb lifetime
numbers.value: 5 s (100 ticks)

numbers.label: Max pickup distance
numbers.value: 70 blocks, same world

numbers.label: Absorption / Health Boost level
numbers.value: 1 + (victim's max health ÷ 16, rounded down), capped at level 51. A 20-HP zombie gives level II.

numbers.label: Absorption / Health Boost duration
numbers.value: 3 min (3600 ticks)

numbers.label: Regeneration
numbers.value: Level VI for 5 s

details.text: Health Boost is only given if the victim had more than 4 max health, so chickens and similar tiny mobs give Absorption only.
Only one orb at a time: a new kill replaces any orb still waiting.

quirks.text: Eating an orb replaces any Absorption you already have (and any Health Boost, if the victim had more than 4 max health), so an orb from a weak mob can replace a stronger effect (like a golden apple's).
If you press F while too far away or in another world, the orb is lost anyway. You get no buffs, it can't be retried, and your hand swap is still cancelled.

foliagewings.summary: An elytra that makes you glow while you wear it. Apart from that, its value is the enchantments.

use.text: Wear it in the chest slot. Glowing is topped up every 3.5 seconds.

numbers.label: Glowing
numbers.value: 17 s per refresh (340 ticks), refreshed every 3.5 s

quirks.text: Taking the wings off removes every Glowing effect you have, including one from a spectral arrow.

marigold-sun-hat.summary: Every 1.5 seconds, the hat pulls nearby dropped items toward you. It reaches 5 blocks at low light levels and up to 8.5 blocks at light level 15.

use.text: Wear it (holding it in either hand also works). Loose items between 3 blocks and the reach limit get pulled toward your head until one of them is close to you.

numbers.label: Check interval
numbers.value: every 1.5 s (30 ticks)

numbers.label: Reach

numbers.label: Ignored if closer than
numbers.value: 3 blocks

numbers.label: Pull duration
numbers.value: up to 7.5 s (150 ticks), or until any item gets within 1.9 blocks of your eyes

details.text: Pulls any dropped item, including other players' drops. It skips a cycle if any item in range is already moving quickly (for example, still falling or already being pulled).

quirks.text: The pull stops for every item as soon as one item reaches you, so items farther out may stop short until the next cycle.

magicwand.summary: A wand with three spells: Boost (a burst of Speed, Jump Boost and Haste), Launch (throws and hurts creatures near where the spell lands) and Clear (blasts a ball of blocks out where it lands). Right-click to cast. Sneak and right-click to switch spells.

use.text: Sneak and right-click to cycle Boost → Launch → Clear. Chat calls them "Boost Effects", "Launch" and "Explosion Sphere".
Right-click to cast. Boost applies straight away. Launch and Clear fire a straight-flying spell orb that goes off where it hits a block or creature.

numbers.label: Boost
numbers.value: Speed III, Jump Boost III, Haste III for 25 s (500 ticks)

numbers.label: Launch radius
numbers.value: 5 blocks around the impact

numbers.label: Launch damage
numbers.value: 5 damage (2.5 hearts) and a fling, repeated 4 times 0.1 s apart

numbers.label: Clear size
numbers.value: a patchy ball up to about 3 blocks in radius (the pattern leaves gaps)

numbers.label: Cooldowns
numbers.value: Boost 30 s, Launch 10 s, Clear 60 s (each separate)

numbers.value: 7.5 s (150 ticks)

details.text: Launch skips creatures you aren't allowed to hurt there (WorldGuard/Towny). Clear only fires if you can build where the spell lands.

quirks.text: Launch and Clear only start their cooldown when the spell actually does something: Launch needs a creature within 5 blocks, Clear needs build permission. Orbs that miss cost nothing, so you can fire them again right away.
Cooldowns are only cleared by a check that runs every 1.5 s while someone is holding a Magic Wand, so a spell can stay locked a little past its listed time.
Launch damage is plain damage with no attacker attached, not an attack from you.

config.text: Clear breaks each block through the server's normal "player breaks a block" action. What drops then follows the game's usual rules for the item in your main hand. The wand is a blaze rod, so blocks that need a pickaxe probably drop nothing. That part is server behaviour, not this plugin's code.

Launch's 4 hits land very close together. Minecraft briefly protects a creature after it's hurt, so the repeat hits probably add little or no damage beyond the first. That depends on the game, not this plugin.

magnitude-wand.summary: Left-click to fire a spell orb. The first creature it hits is resized to a random scale between 0.3× and 2.2×, and hitting a resized creature again returns it to normal. Each successful hit costs 13 lapis.

use.text: Left-click with at least 13 lapis lazuli in your inventory to cast.
If the orb hits a creature that's already been resized, the resize is removed instead.

numbers.label: Cost
numbers.value: 13 lapis, taken only when the orb hits a valid creature

numbers.label: New size
numbers.value: random, from −70% to +120% of normal (0.3× to 2.2×)

numbers.value: 5 s (100 ticks)

details.text: Doesn't work on players, the Ender Dragon or the Wither, or on creatures you aren't allowed to hurt there (WorldGuard/Towny). Those hits cost no lapis.
No cooldown.

quirks.text: Restoring a resized creature to normal size still costs 13 lapis.
Any left-click fires an orb, including hitting a block, and it works with the wand in your off-hand too.

big-dandelion.summary: Holding or wearing the Big Dandelion makes you bigger and makes you jump higher. Right-click to wear it as a hat.

use.text: Hold it in either hand or wear it on your head. Right-clicking with it in your main hand puts it on your head if your helmet slot is empty. You can also place it in the helmet slot from your inventory.

numbers.label: Size
numbers.value: +0.3 scale

details.text: It can't be placed as a flower or put in a composter.
Hard-disabled in the new event world and the Piñata world: you can't switch to it in your hotbar or equip it there.

sticky-taffy.summary: While you hold the taffy and your inventory is too full for an item on the ground, it stuffs that item into a shulker box you're carrying.

use.text: Hold it in your main hand or off-hand and carry at least one shulker box. Walk over items that don't fit in your inventory at all.

numbers.label: Shulker boxes used
numbers.value: 1: the one in your inventory holding the most items

details.text: It only steps in when none of the item fits in your inventory. Shulker boxes themselves are never packed. Whatever doesn't fit in the box stays on the ground.
It isn't instant: the server only runs the check on about one in eleven pickup attempts (counted across all players), so items may take a moment to get packed.

quirks.text: Only your fullest shulker box is ever tried. If that box can't take the item, nothing happens, even if you're carrying an emptier box.

sweet-lollipop.summary: Hold the lollipop in either hand to keep Haste II on you.

use.text: Hold it in your main hand or off-hand. Haste II is topped up every 3.5 seconds.

numbers.label: Haste
numbers.value: Level II, 13 s per refresh (260 ticks), refreshed every 3.5 s

details.text: It can't be placed as a flower.
Haste isn't removed when you put it away. It just runs out, within 13 s.

lumaween-charm.summary: A collectible from the Halloween minigames. It has no ability, so its value is the lore and Unbreaking X.

details.text: The item has no ability code, and nothing else in the plugin refers to it.

config.text: The tooltip hints that keeping it around might pay off. Nothing in this plugin does that, so any such reward would come from another plugin or a staff event.

tahlura-hoe.summary: Right-click to throw a seed that grows into a rain cloud for 15 seconds. Each raindrop ages nearby crops and saplings by one stage. One raindrop in ten is a lightning strike that damages whatever it hits and harvests (then replants) fully grown crops.

use.text: Right-click to lob a slow seed. Where it lands, a column rises 11 blocks and forms the cloud.
The cloud drifts in the direction you're facing, so you can steer it by turning.

numbers.label: Cooldown

numbers.value: within 6 blocks of the cloud centre (square)

numbers.value: up to 1.5 blocks/s (0.075 per tick), slower the further up or down you look

numbers.value: +1 growth stage to plants within 2 blocks

numbers.value: 5 (2.5 hearts) to creatures in a thin column up to the cloud

numbers.value: fully grown crops within 1 block of the strike, dropped as if by a Fortune VIII hoe, then reset to a fresh crop (the same raindrop's growth then usually adds one stage back)

Lightning skips creatures you aren't allowed to hurt there. Otherwise it can hit players and pets, and the damage counts as yours.

autumns-mattock.summary: When you mine an ore, there's a 12% chance it drops 2–5 times its usual loot and a 13% chance it drops nothing. The other 75% of the time it drops normally.

use.text: Mine ores with it in your main hand: any overworld ore (including deepslate), nether gold ore or nether quartz ore. Ancient debris doesn't count.

numbers.label: Surplus drops
numbers.value: 12%: each drop multiplied by a random 2–5 (Fortune still applies first), up to 72 items per drop type

details.text: Only fires on blocks you're actually allowed to break. If protection cancels the break, nothing happens.
Surplus drops spill out one item at a time and don't merge on the ground for about a second.
The ability is disabled in the new event world.

holidayham.summary: Eat the ham to clear out a ball of blocks around you and get Haste III for 30 seconds. It has a 3-minute cooldown and isn't used up.

use.text: Eat it (hold right-click). Solid blocks in a ball around your feet break and drop, and you get Haste III.

numbers.label: Cooldown

numbers.label: Blast size
numbers.value: a ball roughly 5 blocks in radius

numbers.label: Haste
numbers.value: Level III for 30 s (600 ticks)

details.text: Nothing breaks unless you can build at the spot you're standing on (WorldGuard/Towny).

Never breaks chests, barrels, shulker boxes, signs, furnaces, hoppers, brewing stands, droppers, dispensers, spawners, bedrock, portals, farmland, dirt paths and a few other special blocks, and it skips non-solid blocks.
Blocks are broken without a tool, so the ham's own Fortune isn't used for their drops.

The cooldown and Haste apply even when protection stops the blast.
While the ham is in either hand you can't eat or drink anything else: other food and potions are cancelled.

kindlingbaton.summary: Auto-smelts iron, gold and copper ores, ancient debris and sand as you mine them. Press the swap-hands key (F) to flip it between pickaxe and shovel form.

use.text: Press F with it in your main hand to switch between netherite pickaxe and netherite shovel. The hand swap is cancelled.
Mine with it in your main hand. Smeltable blocks drop their smelted result instead.

numbers.label: Smelts

details.text: Fortune still multiplies the drops before they're smelted, so a Fortune roll of 3 raw iron becomes 3 iron ingots.
Only fires on blocks you're allowed to break. The ability is disabled in the new event world.

vigilance-mattock.summary: While the mattock is in your main hand, ores within 3 blocks glow in their ore colour (only you can see this). You're also blinded and most sounds are muted for you.

use.text: Hold it in your main hand. Every tick it checks a 7×7×7 area around you and outlines any ore it finds.

The glow is only visible to you.
Switching slots, swapping it out of your main hand or logging out clears the highlights and removes Blindness.

quirks.text: The tooltip mentions reduced movement, but the only effect the mattock applies is Blindness.
Blindness doesn't check which hand the mattock is in. In your off-hand you still get blinded, but no ores are highlighted.

config.text: The sound muting and the you-only glow both rely on the ProtocolLib plugin. Muting blocks the server's positioned and entity sound effects while the mattock is in your main hand.

equinox-tools.summary: Right-click to scatter 3 geyser seeds around you. Each seed turns into a geyser that fires 5 volleys of balls, and every ball breaks the tool's kind of block where it lands (tree blocks for the Hatchet, shovel blocks for the Spade). The drops fly to you.

use.text: Right-click (works from either hand) to launch 3 seeds outward in random directions.
Each seed that lands becomes a geyser. A geyser fires a volley, waits for every ball to land, pauses about 1 second, and repeats 5 times.

numbers.value: 5 per geyser, 7–11 balls each

The Hatchet and Spade have separate cooldowns.

Each block a ball breaks costs 1 durability from whatever is in your main hand at that moment, so if you've switched items, that item takes the wear.

vigilance-driver.summary: While you hold this crossbow, every creature within 80 blocks glows for you through walls, but you're blinded and most sounds are muted. Each shot also instantly deals 11 damage to the first creature in your line of aim, walls or not.

use.text: Hold it in your main hand or off-hand. Every 3.5 seconds, living things within 80 blocks get a glowing outline that only you see, and you get Blindness.
Fire it. When the shot leaves, the first creature along your aim within 90 blocks takes 11 damage right away, ignoring blocks in between. The arrow itself flies through blocks.

numbers.label: Reveal range

numbers.label: Blindness

Loot from anything you kill appears at your eyes instead of where it died.
Putting it away (neither hand, checked every second) or switching to another hotbar slot removes the glow and Blindness.

quirks.text: You get no experience from anything you kill while the Driver is in either hand, with any weapon. The experience is removed and an empty orb appears instead.
Throwing a trident or ender pearl while the Driver is in either hand deletes it after about half a second: the trident is lost, and a pearl still in the air by then vanishes without teleporting you.
The tooltip mentions reduced movement, but the only effect applied is Blindness.

config.text: The item does no claim or PvP check of its own before the 11-damage hit. Whether it can hurt players or protected mobs depends on the server's protection plugins.
The sound muting (main hand only) and the you-only glow rely on the ProtocolLib plugin.

midnight-claymore.summary: A slow, heavy two-handed sword. Each melee hit also strikes up to 20 creatures around you and your target, and the bonus damage grows with the number of creatures caught.

use.text: Melee-hit something with the Claymore in your main hand and your off-hand empty or holding something that isn't a weapon or tool (a shield is fine).

numbers.label: Area
numbers.value: creatures within 3 blocks of you plus those within 5 blocks of your target, up to 20

numbers.label: Extra damage per creature

numbers.label: Attack speed
numbers.value: −3.5 (replaces the sword's normal −2.4)

numbers.label: Movement speed
numbers.value: −0.01 while in main hand

config.text: The Claymore does no claim or PvP check of its own: every living thing nearby, including other players, pets and villagers, is targeted. Whether they actually take damage is up to the server's protection plugins.

The plugin joins the two nearby-creature lists without removing repeats. If the server's lookup hands back plain lists, a creature close to both you and your target (often the target itself) is counted twice, which raises N and the multiplier. That depends on the server software, so it isn't guaranteed.

honeywickhatchet.summary: Every hit deals 6–14 bonus damage and sometimes sprays decorative honeycomb. Eat the hatchet for 30 seconds of Speed, Regeneration, Absorption and Saturation. The food buff has a 1-minute cooldown and doesn't use up the hatchet.

use.text: Hit something. Bonus damage is added to the hit.
Eat it (hold right-click) for the buffs. If it's still on cooldown, you get a "too full" message.

numbers.value: 1 min (1200 ticks)

details.text: The honeycomb is for show: mobs and hoppers can't pick it up, and it despawns.

quirks.text: Eating is always cancelled: the hatchet isn't used up and restores no hunger itself.
While the hatchet is in either hand you can't eat or drink anything else: other food and potions are cancelled.

nightmare-glaive.summary: When the thrown Glaive lands, it leashes nearby creatures to that spot for 15 seconds and keeps them blinded. While they're held, damage you deal to one of them is copied to all the others.

use.text: Throw it. Where it lands, mobs within 14 blocks and players within 7 blocks are tied to the spot and pulled back if they stray more than about 4 blocks.
Hit any held creature, with any weapon. Every other held creature takes the same damage.

numbers.value: 15 s (300 ticks) for mobs, 5 s for players

A new throw ends your previous hold. If you sneak, every held player (you included) is let go.
Throwing it does nothing in the Piñata world, spawn or the new event world.

quirks.text: You're caught too if you're within 7 blocks of where it lands: pulled in and blinded for 5 seconds unless you sneak.
Copied damage is plain damage with no attacker attached, not an attack from you.

ribbon-socks.summary: While worn, these boots cancel fall damage and freeze (powder snow) damage. The boots take durability damage instead, and they can never fully break.

use.text: Wear them on your feet. The protection only checks the boots slot.

quirks.text: At 1 durability left, the socks stop blocking damage. You take the fall or freeze damage as normal and hear an item-break sound. Repair them to get the protection back (they have no Mending).

config.text: Powder snow usually deals freeze damage 1 point at a time. One third of 1 rounds down to 0, so blocking it should cost no durability (depends on the game, not tested).

wanderers-decanter.summary: Walking or sprinting turns your experience points into Bottles o' Enchanting. Each bottle costs 12 XP points and takes 24 blocks of walking or 32 blocks of sprinting.

use.text: Walk or sprint on foot while wearing the boots. Movement while gliding, flying, riding something or in water doesn't count.

numbers.label: XP cost per bottle
numbers.value: 12 experience points (points, not levels)

numbers.label: Distance per bottle (walking)

numbers.value: Counts as about 1.41 blocks

Stepping back and forth across the same block edge earns nothing. You have to keep moving to new ground.
With under 12 XP points, you get no bottle and your progress stops at one bottle's worth. The next step after you have enough XP makes the bottle.
Walking progress is cleared if you log out while wearing or holding the boots.

quirks.text: The code never checks the boots slot. Carrying the boots in your main hand or off-hand also works while you walk.

paradox-cuirass.summary: A netherite armor piece you can switch between chestplate, leggings, boots and helmet by pressing the swap-hands key. Switching locks for good once you take any damage or die while it's equipped.

use.text: Hold it in your main hand and press the swap-hands key (F). It changes piece in place and stays in your main hand. The order is chestplate, leggings, boots, helmet, then back to chestplate.

numbers.label: Cooldown between switches
numbers.value: 0.5 s (10 ticks)

details.text: Damage from any source locks switching if the cuirass is worn in any armor slot or held in either hand, and so does dying. When damage locks it, you see soul particles and hear a sound.
Once it's locked, pressing F does a normal hand swap.

quirks.text: The lock applies to you as a player, not to one cuirass, and nothing in the item ever removes it. It lasts until the server restarts or staff clear your cooldowns with the plugin's clear-cooldown command.

config.text: Switching only changes the item's type, so its enchantments and name should carry over to each piece (depends on the game, not tested).

amor-ceralytras.summary: An elytra that adds two sneak-triggered air jumps and a charged high launch. Press sneak in mid-air to jump again, or hold sneak on the ground for 4 seconds and release to launch upward.

use.text: In mid-air, press sneak to jump again toward where you're looking. You get up to 2 of these before you touch the ground.
On the ground, hold sneak. After 4 seconds a bell plays and red dust appears. Let go of sneak (or leave the ground) to launch high into the air.

numbers.label: Air jumps

Stand still while charging the high launch. Moving along the ground resets the 4-second count.

quirks.text: The code never checks the chestplate slot, so both abilities also work with the elytra held in either hand.

deep-rose-veil.summary: While you wear this elytra, you have the Glowing effect with a dark purple outline.

strawberry-chapeau.summary: Kills give you saturation, up to your current food level. Once per hour it also saves you from death and revives you with 15 health (7.5 hearts).

use.text: Wear it and kill mobs to top up your saturation. The hat takes a little durability each time.

quirks.text: Neither ability checks that the hat is on your head. Both also work with it held in either hand. The durability cost always goes to whatever is in your helmet slot, not to the hat.

hearthglow-lantern.summary: While you hold it, nearby mobs and animals keep the Glowing effect. Players and armor stands are not affected.

infinite-milk-bucket.summary: A milk bucket that stays full after you drink it. Drinking still clears your effects like normal milk.

reformation-pouch-bundle.summary: A sealed pouch. Right-clicking it uses it up and gives you one Reformation Pouch for a random wood type.

reformation-pouches.summary: A bundle that turns wood items put inside it into the pouch's own wood type. For example, birch planks placed in a cherry pouch become cherry planks.

Crimson and warped (nether) wood, azalea leaves and anything else not listed stay as they are.
Stack sizes and item names are kept. Only the wood type changes.
Each fill converts every Reformation Pouch in your inventory and in any container you have open, not just the one you used.
Crafting a pouch with one dye recolours it and keeps its wood type and contents. No other items can be in the grid.

prism-pearl.summary: Right-click to teleport the nearest passive animal within 40 blocks to you. It can't be thrown like an ender pearl.
